Motion compensation is a well-known technique to mitigate the effects of vibration of the movement. In this paper, we study how the power spectrum of a vibration profile affects the coherency within a pulse and between the pulses. Based on the observations, we propose a method to determine the need for the use of a motion compensation algorithm in a coherent homodyne radar.

articleTitle: Phase unwrapping based on weighted bipartite matching
abstract: Two-dimensional phase unwrapping (PU) is a key technique in many scientific fields. In this paper, the L<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub>-norm-based PU is implemented via a novel method, which is simpler than the classic minimum-cost network flow (MCF) method. It is proved that the network associated with the PU problem can be simplified to a weighted bipartite graph, and matching this graph can solve the PU problem with higher efficiency than the MCF method. Tests on the simulated data and the real InSAR data confirm that the proposed method has a much lower computing complexity than the traditional MCF method.

articleTitle: Precession period estimation of ballistic target in midcourse
abstract: To solve the problem of inaccuracy and bad anti-noise performance in traditional methods on precession period estimation, a novel approach is suggested. The approach is based on the exploiting average magnitude difference function (AMDF) and autocorrelation function (ACF). No a priori information about ballistic target under classification is required for estimation of period. The trend term of AMDF is eliminated after empirical mode decomposition (EMD) processes. Then the ACF is used to weight the new AMDF. Thus the new feature is constructed to estimate precession period. Synthetic data of ballistic target is used both for performance evaluation of suggested and traditional approaches. The benefit of suggested approach comparing to traditional approaches is demonstrated using the mean square errors of precession period estimates computed in additive noise environment.

articleTitle: Optimization of polyphase codes based on weighted cyclic algorithm for synthetic aperture radar
abstract: Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) can bring high range and azimuth resolutions, and is valuable to military and civil usage. Corresponding to the problem that SAR can be easily affected by deceptive jamming, one method based on multiple orthogonal phase codes jittered between neighboring pulses is proposed to anti jamming. Based on Weighted Cyclic Algorithm, long polyphase codes are optimized and then peak of the codes' correlation function is increased. The sidelobes of correlation function as well as the peak of cross-correlation function are decreased with the method. Simulation testified the performance of the method through comparison with the performance of biphase code.

articleTitle: An effective method for designing near-field MIMO array
abstract: The three-dimensional (3-D) imaging technique based on array antenna is an important way to achieve a 3-D image. However, conventional imaging radar system requires a large number of antenna elements. Both the cost and complexity of the system are increased. This paper refers to the principle of MIMO radar and introduces a near-filed optimization method for sparse array designing based on the equivalent phase center principle and convolution principle. Using the method introduced in this paper, the array can use less real elements to get unambiguous image. Simulations are provided to demonstrate the performance of the proposed method, which proves that it is an effective way to solve the near-field sparse array designing problem.

articleTitle: Context segmentation of oceanic SAR images: Application to oil spill detection
abstract: This paper introduces an algorithm based on the context of MRF (Markov random field) model, and this method achieved oil spilling detection and segmentation. In this paper, the two important elements are initial labelling field and potential parameter estimation. The algorithm model chooses optical pyramid of saliency map as initial label field and Ising model as segmentation function. Using the GMM (Gaussian Mixture Model) and MAP (Maximum a Posterior) get local optimal result by ICM (Iteration Condition Model) method. This paper is also deeply researching the potential parameter which is the impact factor in segmentation function. Through studying the relationship between potential function and every scale-levels of saliency pyramid, the paper gets the better result which is more accuracy segmentations and keeping more texture information. The series experiments prove this method having false alarming rejection and noise suppression function in Oceanic SAR images.

articleTitle: Multi-target localization using geometric model for distributed MIMO radar
abstract: The multi-target localization method for distributed multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar is investigated in this paper. A geometric-model-based method is proposed for multi-target localization and it is still efficient in the case when some targets with multiple spatial reflections become unobservable in some transmitter-receiver channels. Weight coefficients are used to determine the position of targets. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method effectively accomplishes multi-target localization with the distributed MIMO radar across scattering cross-section (RCS) and it outperforms the existing method both at search time and localization accuracy.

articleTitle: SAR image edge detection based on fuzzy theory and information fusion
abstract: Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) image edge detection is one of the important steps for earth observation and target recognition,and it is recognized a difficult problem by domestic and foreign researchers because of the presence of speckle noise. A study was undertaken in this paper to speckle noise suppression and edge detail holding for SAR image edge detection, and we present an intelligent edge detection approach based on fuzzy theory and information fusion. Some typical SAR images were selected for edge detection using this approach in order to verify the result of relevant speckle noise suppression and edge detail holding. Results shows that this method can effectively inhibit the SAR image speckle noise and has smart edge detection ability. Unlike classical SAR image edge detection methods, this approach is a comprehensive integrated of different intelligent information processing methods, and it shows good robustness and universality.

articleTitle: Communication performance optimization of spaceborne/airborne radar networks
abstract: In this paper, we investigate communication performance optimization problem of spaceborne/airborne Radar networks. A model of spaceborne/airborne Radar networks with propagation delay and power constraints is given first. A Quadric Lyapunov function based Algorithm (QLA) is then proposed aiming at greedily minimizing an expression containing Lyapunov drift. We prove two main conclusions, one is that the communication network of spaceborne/airborne Radars under QLA is stable, the other is that power constraints are met. Upper bounds of queue backlogs and a lower bound of utility function are established through theoretical analysis, and how propagation delay jeopardizes utility performance is also demonstrated. Simulation of QLA is carried out in a scenario consists of 6 nodes, and results are in accordance with theoretical conclusions.

articleTitle: Analysis of large waveguide slotted antenna array using symmetry techniques
abstract: This paper discusses the simulation of Ka band large waveguide slotted antenna array using symmetry based on higher-order Method of Moment (MoM). Compared with the traditional MoM, higher-order MoM largely reduce the unknowns of the problem and makes it possible for us to simulate the large waveguide slotted antenna array with high accuracy. The symmetry technique make the problem reduce to half or even a quarter for the symmetry objects, thus the compute time and storage are largely decreased. Moreover, the using of parallel calculation further accelerates the solving speed. Numerical examples are presented to prove the efficient of this method.

articleTitle: The estimation for the direction of arrival based on sparse array
abstract: The estimation method for the Direction of Arrival problem based on compressed sensing is proposed. In the case of sparse array antenna, the receiving signal from absence elements can be reconstructed by using the theory of compressed sensing. In this work, we set the scene that the antenna elements reduce greatly. But we can still estimate the result almost the same with the result of full array antenna by sparse sampling. Simulation results show that this method can rebuild the data well.

articleTitle: A tracking algorithm based on association probability for radar against deceptive chaff
abstract: This paper proposes a new tracking algorithm for radar based on association probability of each observation to confront deceptive chaff. When deceptive chaff is released, conventional tracking algorithm such as nearest neighbour which keeps only a single hypothesis may lose efficacy once it chooses false target. Hence the possibility of every observation coming from real target is taken into account in the proposed method. The association probability of observations has been discussed at length, and the tracking algorithm using Kalman filter with association probability as weights is proposed. The performance of the proposed algorithm is validated by numerical simulation, which outperforms the conventional algorithms especially when deceptive chaff existed.

articleTitle: 3-D imaging of spaceborne distributed SAR based on phase preserving compressive sensing
abstract: Spaceborne multi-static synthetic aperture radar (SAR) with different baselines extends the synthetic aperture principle of monostatic SAR into the elevation direction for 3-D imaging. In this paper, an expression of 3-D SAR echo data is presented. To meet the requirements of 3-D imaging, a phase preserving compressive sensing approach is proposed to solve the ground reflectivity. Simulation experiments indicate that the phase of raw complex signal is well preserved and the 3-D image of interested area is reconstructed efficiently.

articleTitle: Segmentation of oil spills in SAR image based on improved CV model
abstract: Extracting the oil spills in SAR images has been challenged by the spatial heterogeneity caused by the speckles. In this paper, we present a novel variational formulation based on the local characteristics of SAR images for CV mode. The proposed method is aimed to solve the segmentation problem caused by SAR image speckles. Compared with the traditional CV model, the performance of the improved CV model is verified by plenty of real airborne SAR images and the experimental results on the real data show its efficiency and accuracy. By presenting various results in the classical threshold segmentation method and Markov random field method respectively, we conclude that the improved CV model is effective and accurate.

articleTitle: Simulation of an airplane using parallel PO method on supercomputer platform with 100000 CPU cores
abstract: Parallel physical optics (PO) method is used to simulate the scattering pattern of an airplane on the National Supercomputing Center in Jinan, which is a purely domestic supercomputer with intellectual property rights. Furthermore, some benchmarks about parallel efficiency of the parallel code are tested on this supercomputer platform. The results indicate that an almost perfectly performance can be obtained when using up to 100000 CPU cores.

articleTitle: Estimation of target polarization parameters based on particle swarm optimizer
abstract: In this paper, a new algorithm to estimate target's polariza-tion parameters is proposed based on particle swarm optimi-zer (PSO). Here, two mutually orthogonal coded waveforms are transmitted in the same frequency simultaneously with horizontal and vertical polarizations respectively. Then, the returns are received by horizontal and vertical polarizations channels in the meantime. Finally, PSO is used to estimate the polarization parameters of target, which can suppress the errors caused by the cross-correlation noise between two transmitted waveforms. And numerical experiments are provided to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Manmade target extraction in PolSAR data using polarimetric coherence optimization
abstract: Polarimetric coherence strongly relates to the types and orientations of local scatterers. An optimization scheme is proposed to optimize the coherence between two polarimetric channels for polarimetric SAR (PolSAR) data. The coherence magnitude (correlation coefficient) is maximized by rotating a polarimetric coherency matrix in the rotation domain around the radar line of sight. Pi-SAR data sets are used for demonstration and validation. The coherence of oriented manmade targets is significantly enhanced while that of forests remains relatively low. Therefore, the proposed technique can effectively discriminate these two land covers which are easily misinterpreted by the conventional model-based decomposition. Moreover, based on an optimized polarimetric coherence parameter and the total backscattered power, a simple manmade target extraction scheme is developed for application demonstration. This approach is applied with the Pi-SAR data. The experimental results validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A new parameter estimation algorithm for fast moving targets
abstract: A new parameter estimation algorithm based on Sub-band Dual Frequency Conjugate and LVT (SDFC-LVT) operation is proposed for fast moving targets. A new synthetic signal is constructed by the essential operations, including spectrum division, frequency shifting, and conjugate multiplications. After that, Keystone transform and LVT operator are performed on the constructed signal to attain the estimates. Since the equivalent carrier frequency is reduced greatly, the proposed method is capable of obtaining the accurate parameter estimates and resolving the problem of ambiguity which invalidates Keystone transform. It is more suitable for the situation of multiple targets. Several simulation examples demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A fully coherent motion compensation method of ISAR imaging based on synthetic wideband PD radar
abstract: In order to solve the problem of accurate motion compensation of ISAR imaging, and get high quality ISAR images, this paper proposes a fully coherent motion compensation method based on synthetic wideband PD radar. The method adopts phase derived velocity measurement (PDVM) based on range profile cross-correlation (RPCC) that enables it to accurately estimate the instantaneous target velocity , which is an important benefit of the excellent coherence characteristics of the synthetic wideband PD radar. Applying the estimated velocity to envelope alignment and translational phase adjustment process of ISAR imaging, we finally get high quality ISAR images. The experimental results of ISAR imaging on aircrafts verify that the proposed method is effective.

articleTitle: A heterogeneous clutter suppression method based on subarrays
abstract: Most fighter aircraft is equipped with forward looking radar. The forward looking radar worked at the medium or high pulse repetition frequency causes ambiguous clutter and an elevation dependent angle-Doppler relationship in the clutter returns. The heterogeneity induced by shortrange and ambiguous clutter will degrade the adaptive clutter suppress performance. A heterogeneous clutter suppression method for forward looking airborne radar based on subarrays is proposed in this paper. The proposed method can use subarray elevation degrees of freedom to improve the performance in heterogeneous clutter circumstance and simultaneously reduce system complexity and computation load. Simulation results show that the proposed method outperforms the conventional method and can improve heterogeneous clutter suppression performance dramatically.

articleTitle: Discrimination and identification of time-delay repeater jamming and target echo by basis pursuit
abstract: The basis pursuit algorithm of sparse decomposition is used to recover and discriminate the target echo and the jamming signal which have different time-delay and pulse width. The key is to construct an atomic dictionary. The recoveries in both the noiseless case and in the noisy case are considered. The noiseless case adopts linear programming. The noisy case adopts quadratic programming. Since the recovery is sensitive to the noise, the solution to the noisy case is unstable. More importantly, densely false targets, including the case that two signals are overlapped in the temporal domain, can also be recovered. Finally, simulations verifies the results.

articleTitle: A decomposition-based sensor scheduling procedure in radar networks
abstract: This paper addresses the sensor resource scheduling problem that allocating the radar resources to track targets under the time and energy constrains in the multi-radar system. The objective is to maximize the number of the targets which can be tracked and improve the utilization of the sensor resources. The optimal scheduling problem with maximize the tracking number and matching number is developed. We then proposed a decomposition-based procedure to solve the problem. It decomposes the bi-objective problem into two sub-problems and solves the two sub-problems optimally with the implicit enumeration method. The simulation results show that the proposed method improves the overall capacity of a multi-radar system compared to the existing techniques.

articleTitle: Fixed-point simulation technology for SAR real-time imaging system
abstract: In this paper, a fast fixed-point simulation technology is proposed for a multi-channel synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imaging system. The overall computations in the SAR imaging algorithm is explicitly analysed. FFT operations account for most memory consumption in the imaging flow. Accordingly, a fixed-point FFT algorithm is adopted due to the trade-off between precision and memory occupation of the FPGA implementation. Furthermore, this paper describes an optimized word-length configuration method based on theoretical analysis of architecture of Radix-22 FFT. This methodology is verified in a SystemC development environment due to its superiority of fast and bit-accurate system-level simulation capability. Finally, the proposed SystemC based fixed-point imaging algorithm and the Matlab based floating-point imaging algorithm are both conducted to process point array target raw data. Peak side-lobe ratio (PSLR) and integrated side-lobe ratio (ISLR) is evaluated. Experimental results indicate that profiles in the two cases do not differ greatly, which validates that the proposed fixedpoint algorithm with less resources occupation has comparable accuracy and can meet system requirements.

articleTitle: Periodic non-uniformly sampled signal reconstruction of FMCW MIMO SAR using fractional fourier transform
abstract: Compared to pulse SAR, Frequency-Modulated Continuous-Wave Synthetic Aperture Radar (FMCW SAR) is much smaller and lighter. To realize the high-resolution wide-swath SAR imaging and greatly reduce the transmitted power restriction for FMCW SAR, Multiple Input Multiple Output (MIMO) technology is used to realize Multiple Azimuth Beams (MAB). However, when the platform velocity deviates from the theoretical speed, the azimuth signals will be periodic non-uniformly sampled, producing ambiguous targets in azimuth direction. In this paper, the FMCW MIMO SAR non-uniformly sampled signal is presented and the periodic non-uniformly sampled signal reconstruction algorithm based on Fractional Fourier Transform (FrFT) is proposed. Finally, simulation results show the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

Author Keywords: Frequency-Modulated Continuous-Wave Synthetic Aperture Radar (FMCW SAR)

articleTitle: Deformation monitoring in Shanghai maglev area
abstract: As a very fast traffic tool, the stability of the roadbed of Shanghai maglev is very important. However, the geological condition in Shanhai is very poor and the ground subsidence is severe. So, it is necessary to monitor ground subsidence in the area along the maglev precisely. For half a century, precise levelling method has been used to survey the ground subsidence in Shanghai. But the levelling points are so sparse that we can not get the regional ground subsidence information in details. The emergence of differential synthetic aperture radar interferometry (DInSAR) technology make up for this deficiency, which can detect ground subsidence in a wide area. Over the past decade, DInSAR comes into playing a valuable part in monitoring ground subsidence. Especially, small baseline differential SAR(SBAS) technique based on DInSAR technology can get the useful deformation using only a few radar images. In this paper, ENVISAT ASAR data are used to extract ground subsidence information using SBAS method in Shanghai maglev area. The results show that there is no significant ground subsidence on the maglev line. There are a few places with significant local subsidence rates at about -20mm/y near the railway line.

articleTitle: CS-CORR range super-resolution method for stepped frequency HF radar system
abstract: In HF (high frequency) radar, the discontinuous spectrum is a key obstacle for the range resolution enhancement because of the bandwidth limitation. For increasing the signal effective bandwidth as much as possible, the sparse stepped frequency signal is emerged. However, the conventional correlation processing method for this signal will produce high sidelobe, this paper proposes CS-CORR method and deduced the resolution function. The main idea of this new method is to joint existing compressive sensing (CS) and correlation function (CORR) method. This method can reconstruct the sparse frequency and obtain the estimation of non-sparse frequency structure; also it can reduce the sidelobe interference brought by conventional methods, and further realize the effect of super-resolution.

articleTitle: Calculate the polarized scattering properties of canted rain media with M-P DSD using extended Mie scattering method
abstract: In this paper, an extended Mie scattering method is proposed to calculate the scattered field of randomly canted ellipsoid raindrops. In this method, the ellipsoid raindrop is stretched to a sphere and the coordinate system is rotated to meet the regular condition, then the Mie scattering method is employed to calculate the scattered field. Based on the method, simulations on the different raindrop sizes and canted angles show that, 1) for non-canted raindrops the scattered amplitude turns out to be a function of the droplet sizes, but 2) the scattered field of uniformly canted raindrops is mainly determined by the canted angles. Comparison of the simulation results for different angles and rainfall rates with the reported measurement data in Tsingtao shows the good performance of the method, and further analysis of the relationship between the effective propagation constant and the rainfall rate as well as the raindrop's canted angles is also presented. According to the equivalence between the canted angle and polarization mode, the effects caused by polarization are also analyzed.

articleTitle: Interface conversion and extension based on FPGA in high-speed real-time signal processing system
abstract: The radar systems have been so significant for both civil use and national defense, and adopting localized processor has become critical for a country, especially for the area related to the national defense. In this paper, we utilize localized BWDSP100 as the main processor, and implement a high-speed and real-time signal processing system by using BWDSP100 + FPGA framework. We use FPGA to realize the interface conversions and extensions, which enhance the reading bandwidth of the DDR2 interface from 235MB/s to 562MB/s. Besides that, we also integrate highspeed serial buses, such as PCIe interface of 243MB/s and SRIO interface of 344MB/s, for communications in or between boards. The system has been used in several projects, and works well.

articleTitle: Research on amplitude-phase error for LFMCW radar
abstract: FMCW radar with deramping technique has many advantages comparing to traditional pulse radar. But the expressing of signal error becomes more complicated. The distortions on amplitude and phase are unavoidable for wide bandwidth and wide pulse signal, which have a serious impact on the imaging quality. Aiming at the problem of signal error correction, the echo signal model of FMCW radar with amplitude-phase error was established in this paper. The analysis of error estimation and correction were investigated in detail especially for non-linear phase error. And a practical solution was presented to reduce the effects from the distortions. The processing and results were proved through theoretical derivation and simulation analysis validation. And this method has significantly improved the range resolution and calibrated the position deviation. Additionally, this algorithm has a strong practicability, due to considering both the indicator and real-time imaging processing algorithm costs.

articleTitle: ESB-DMR beamforming under random matrix theory judgment principle
abstract: Eigenspace-based beamformer and dominant mode rejection are robust against DOA mismatch and array model mismatch when SNR is proper. While the former algorithm suffers from performance break down at low SNR and at high SNR, the performance of the latter degrades. We propose a principle to judge the level of the SNR based on random matrix theory. The idea of random matrix theory is to identify the level of subspace swap phenomenon, which is closely related to input SNR. With the principle we are able to combine two methods together and both effectiveness and robustness of proposed principle are demonstrated by simulation results.

articleTitle: A novel coherent integration algorithm for moving target
abstract: For better detection of weak moving target, a novel coherent integration algorithm is proposed in this paper. The received signal of each period is firstly transformed from fast-time domain to frequency domain. Then non-uniform fast Fourier transform (NUFFT) is utilized in slow-time domain to compensate the phase fluctuation entailed by range migration. Inverse fast Fourier transform (IFFT) in fast-time frequency domain is finally applied for the completion of integration. Compared with the existing coherent integration algorithms, the computational complexity of the proposed algorithm is much lower without loss of integration performance. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Antenna beam-null arrangement based on time-direction pattern by knowledge-aided method
abstract: In traditional adaptive nulling antennae, the beam-nulls come into being perfectly for stationary jamming signals. But their ability of nulling will be severely weakened for nonstationary jamming signals so that the target detection performance becomes worse for radar. In this paper the new conception of time-direction pattern for radars is introduced, in which the information for direction change with time is obtained by direction finding for all spatial signals continuously. Under the inferential rules given by the knowledge, the nonstationary jamming signals are discerned, and their directions of arrival can be deduced by histogram projection and statistic process for the time-direction pattern. Then the fixed beam-nulls are arranged for those jamming directions according to above result. The adaptive nulling is next used for the other jamming leavings. In this way, all kinds of jamming signals in space can be eliminated greatly. Simulation results are given to support the validity of our scheme.

articleTitle: Covariance matrix tapers estimation in knowledge-aided STAP for sea clutter environment
abstract: In knowledge-aided space-time adaptive processing (KASTAP), a priori knowledge of the clutter covariance matrix is incorporated to enhance the radar detection performance in heterogeneous environment. In KA-STAP under sea clutter environment, the internal clutter motion (ICM) cannot be neglected, so it is necessary to estimate the covariance matrix taper (CMT) of the a priori covariance matrix according to real time clutter state. Traditionally, CMT is modelled as a singer function, which is not suitable in sea clutter environment for its lacking of adaptability. In this paper, we develop a CMT directly data estimation approach (DDE), where ICM information is extracted from training samples and used to construct CMT. By utilizing real time extracted information, the DDE CMT approach has the ability to cognitive time-varying sea clutter environment. Simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed CMT estimation approach.

articleTitle: Imaging plane characterisation for ISAR imaging of LEO space objects
abstract: For inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) imaging of low earth orbit (LEO) space objects, the study of the variations in the imaging plane of the object in the entire visible arc period can acquire a more direct vision of the variations in object imaging. In this study, the ideal turntable model was extended to establish the observation geometry of LEO near circular orbit objects. Two approximations were applied to the observation model in the calculation of the imaging plane normal for near circular orbit objects. One approximation is to treat the orbit of the space object as a standard arc relative to the earth during the radar observation period. The other approximation is to omit the effect of the rotation of the earth on the observations. First, the closed-form solution of the imaging plane normal in various attitude stabilisation approaches was acquired based on geometry models. Then, the correctness of the closed-form solution for the geometric models and the effect of various attitude-stabilisation methods on ISAR imaging were confirmed by simulations.

articleTitle: Translation motion and period estimation for precession targets
abstract: The micro-motion is combined with the high velocity of translation motion for ballistic targets. The translation motion should be compensated for micro-Doppler information extraction. A new method based on delay conjugate multiplication to estimate the translation motion parameters and precession period jointly is proposed in this paper. By delay conjugate multiplication of the received signal, the micro-Doppler information can be cancel out when the delay time is corresponding to the precession period and the translation motion parameters estimation problem is transformed to a multi-polynomial phase signal parameters estimation problem. Based on this character, an algorithm to estimate the translation motion and precession period parameters is proposed. Simulation results indicate that the proposed algorithm can achieve high-precision parameters estimate performance for ballistic targets under low SNR.

articleTitle: Angular resolution performance analysis for HF-MIMO radar
abstract: High frequency surface wave radar (HFSWR) is a kind of effectively detecting target over the sea horizon radar system which has been widely used because of excellent performance. Taking the advantages of Multiple Input Multiple Output (MIMO) radar's technology, new optimized HF-MIMO radar is introduced in this paper which promotes the Woodward's ambiguity functions to HF-MIMO radar and produces original ambiguity functions for HF-MIMO radar. Through the ambiguity functions, angular resolution ability is investigated carefully. In the cases of monostatic radar and bistatic radar, formula and influencing factors of HF-MIMO radar's ambiguity functions are given and angular resolution's abilities are shown by finding HF-MIMO perfect resolution in large aperture.

articleTitle: An azimuth weighting method of slide-spotlight SAR based on subaperture chirp scaling algorithm
abstract: Different azimuth targets have different Doppler centroid and different time support domain in slide spotlight synthetic aperture radar. Thus, it is hard to weighting window on the echo in slide spotlight mode. This paper proposed an azimuth weighting method of slide spotlight SAR based on subaperture chirp scaling algorithm. Firstly, the subaperture number of the algorithm is discussed based on the shift of Doppler centroid and the pulse repetition frequency(PRF). Secondly, the range cell migration and the remove of the azimuth phase of each subaperture are processed by chirp scaling algorithm independently. At last, the data of each subaperture is combined together, and the azimuth weighting window is applied after an azimuth de-ramp process of the combined data. The computer simulations verify the validity of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Adaptive multiple cues integration for particle filter tracking
abstract: Visual object tracking in complex environments is a challenging task in smart surveillance fields. In order to enhance the robust tracking performance, many tracking algorithms based on multi cues integration have been proposed. However, how the multiple cues are fused during tracking is still an open issue. This paper integrates multiple cues into particle filtering framework for robust tracking in situations where no single cue is suitable. A novel quality function is introduced to evaluate the reliability of each cue. With the weights corresponding to the cue reliabilities, the combined likelihood is estimated as the weighted average of each cue. Experiments show that tracking with multiple weighted cues provides more reliable performance than single cue tracking.

articleTitle: Modified GLRT detector with limit of loaded sample matrix inversion
abstract: The problem of signal detection in unknown Gaussian interference with an adaptive array is considered in this paper. A modified Generalized Likelihood Ratio Test (GLRT) detector is suggested to improve the performance of Kelly's GLRT, when the sample that estimating the covariance matrix is limited. The modified GLRT detector proposed in this paper is noiseless unloaded GLRT (NUGLRT). Advantages of the proposed detector are illustrated by simulations comparing with some typical diagonalloaded detectors.

articleTitle: Modified Rao test for adaptive subspace detection
abstract: The problem of detecting a subspace signal is studied in colored Gaussian noise with an unknown covariance matrix. In the subspace model, the target signal belongs to a known subspace, but with unknown coordinates. We first present a new derivation of the Rao test based on the subspace model, and then propose a modified Rao test (MRT) by introducing a tunable parameter. The MRT is more general, which includes the Rao test and the generalized likelihood ratio test as special cases. Numerical results demonstrate that the MRT can offers the flexibility of being adjustable in the mismatched case where the target signal deviates from the presumed signal subspace. In particular, the MRT provides better mismatch rejection capacities as the tunable parameter increases.

articleTitle: Analysis of background ionospheric effects on low frequency repeat-pass InSAR system
abstract: This paper presents an analysis of the background ionospheric effects on the repeat-pass interferometric SAR. The analysis is mainly related to the ionospheric dispersive phase and Faraday Rotation (FR). The background ionosphere results in both the deterioration of coherence and the interferometric phase error. This will affect the performance of height measurement for InSAR systems. The theoretical derivation and analyses of these two ionospheric characteristics are presented, followed by the performance calculations of spaceborne InSAR systems using typical parameters.

articleTitle: Preliminary results of the metasensing fully polarimetric L-band airborne SAR for vegetation classification
abstract: In this paper some preliminary results on the classification of vegetation by means of the MetaSensing L-band fully polarimetric airborne radar sensor are shown. A test flight has been performed over two selected areas in the Netherlands, where ground truth surveys have been done to validate the outcome of the classification. The classification procedure is based on a eigenvalue/eigenvector decomposition of the coherency matrix of the fully polarimetric SAR data.

articleTitle: RF imperfections compensation for wavelet-based multi-band spectrum sensing
abstract: Cognitive radio (CR) techniques are used widely to improve the utilization of spectrum resources by allocating spectrum holes dynamically. The spectrum sensing is one of the key CR techniques, especially for wideband cognitive radio. It has been the main emphasis of a lot of researches in CR communications. The wavelet transform detection method can divide the wideband spectrum, and then comparing the estimated energy of the each band with the threshold to determine whether the presence of a primary users (PU) signal or not. However, for the direct conversion receivers, because of its structure and hardware defects, there are a variety of RF front-end damages, especially in-phase/quadrature (IQ) imbalance. These problems not only result in the mirror-frequency cross-talk but also cause the errors to divide the wideband spectrum, finally considerably degrading the sensing performance. Thus in this paper a simple fast and effective solution was proposed, the Fourier series coefficients based compensation (FC) method. The position of the residual image bands can be locked by the Fourier series coefficients so that it can completely eliminate the residual image bands, and make the wideband detection getting a better result. Extensive computer simulations with two type of signals and various imbalance conditions are provided. It demonstrated that the proposed algorithm can eliminate the image channel cross-talk efficiently, yielding detection and false alarm probabilities essentially identical to those of an ideal RF receiver.

articleTitle: Multifractal spectrum features based classification method for aircraft
abstract: The multifractal spectrum characteristics of aircraft echoes from low-resolution radars offer a fine description of dynamic characteristics which induce the echo structure; therefore they can provide a new way for aircraft target classification and recognition with low-resolution radars. On basis of introducing the elementary theory of multifractal, the paper analyzed the multifractal spectrum characteristics of aircraft echoes along with the extraction method of their multifractal spectrum features by means of the multifractal analysis of measures, and proposed the classification method for different types of aircraft targets from the viewpoint of pattern classification. The results of classification experiments with real recorded echo data showed the multifractal-spectrum-feature-based classification method can classify different types of aircraft effectively, thus. the defined characteristic parameters could be used as effective features for aircraft target classification.

articleTitle: A PC software design for monitoring receiver of BeiDou navigation satellite system
abstract: Satellite navigation monitoring receiver makes it possible that navigation system can provide high-reliability and high-precise measurement data. In this paper, the Personal Computer (PC) software controls the work status of a receiver. Therefore, it is necessary to design a reliable PC software for receiver working. This paper proposes a programming method with Microsoft Foundation Classes (MFC) of PC software for monitoring receiver which monitors the BeiDou Navigation Satellite System (BDS) of new civil signal. PC software reads the data from NPort and necessary information can be exactly displayed on the interface. Besides, the information can also be saved as a specified file. Compared to the traditional serial port, data can be transmitted by more than one port simultaneously through NPort. It has been proved that this method makes the transmission more effective than the traditional serial port.

articleTitle: High-accuracy radar calibration based on ADS-B
abstract: A novel radar error calibration method is proposed to easier calibrate the high-accuracy radar, which is based on the dynamic correction of the ADS-B fixed error and the change of the target echo center. Firstly, the source, types and the characteristics under radar coordinate system of ADS-B position data error are analyzed. Secondly, a model of the change of aviation target echo center is established and analyzed. Finally, on the basis, the radar systematic errors are estimated through a dynamic joint correction is done to the difference of radar data and ADS-B data. This method can improve the precision and stability of the estimation of radar systematic error. Multiple batches measured data is used to test and verify the novel method, and also used to compare performance with other methods. The result indicated that this method effectively improved the precision and stability of the radar systematic error calibration, and the method is succeeded applying in radar calibration equipment.

articleTitle: A new region growing based method for ship detection in high-resolution SAR images
abstract: High-resolution SAR are of great value in remote sensing nowadays. To make good use of the characteristics of high-resolution SAR images to detect targets, we present here a region growing method. First, we calculate a threshold according to the given PFA to pick up bright pixels as the seeds. Second, we define the criteria which is mainly based on the relationship between pixels in a high -resolution SAR image and then execute the growing process. Finally, we exclude false alarms according to some geometry features. The experiments and results show that it is a constructive and effective way using region growing algorithm to detect ships in high-resolution SAR images.

articleTitle: An improved adaptive monopulse estimation algorithm based on a modified subspace tracking technique
abstract: In this paper, an improved adaptive monopulse scheme based on modified projection approximation subspace tracking deflation (MPASTd) approach is proposed. Owing to the fast convergence speed of MPASTd for recursively estimating the interference subspace, the proposed algorithm can obtain the formula for adaptive monopulse ratio calculation by a subspace projection. Therefore, it is able to accurately estimate the source location using less training data and reduce the computational complexity significantly. The effectiveness and fast convergence speed of the proposed method is verified by simulation results.

articleTitle: Extended target tracking with particle filtering in coherent MIMO radar
abstract: In this paper, we address the problem of detecting and tracking a target suffering from the appearance of grating lobes with reference to array radar system. Array radar technique is used to improve azimuth resolution with large equivalent aperture. But the need of larger equivalent aperture requires more array elements and/or longer spacing between elements, and then leads to the appearance of grating lobes Target tracking performance, in this case, will suffer serious decrease due to the appearance of grating lobes as the spacing between array elements increasing beyond a half wavelength. There are lots of methods for reducing grating lobes up to the present. However, these methods did not make the most of grating lobes. As grating lobes are shadows of a target, they reveal the position of target implicitly. With evaluating the area of grating lobes and adding these piece of information into tracking algorithm, target signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) can be improved equivalently. In this work, we propose an effective PF-TBD algorithm exploiting grating lobes for target detection and tracking. Simulation results show that tracking performance can be dramatically increased when the usually discarded information is taken in count.

articleTitle: A Gaussian mixture Converted Doppler Measurement Kalman Filter
abstract: A new linear filter, the Converted Doppler Measurement Kalman Filter (CDMKF) has been previously presented to extract nonlinear pseudo-state from converted Doppler measurements (i.e., the product of the range measurements and Doppler measurements). Inherent in this filter is a nonGaussian and more complicated pseudo-states noise, although the pseudo-states evolve linearly in time. A Gaussian mixture estimation algorithm (GM-CDMKF) is developed in this paper to alleviate the deteriorated filtering performance due to the non-Gaussian process noise without too much computational expenses. Monte Carlo simulations are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of the GMCDMKF.

articleTitle: European space surveillance bistatic breadboard radar
abstract: A bistatic radar demonstrator representative of a future ground based radar system in a realistic operational environment has been developed and realized by ONERA, prime in a consortium of European companies with the support of ESA (European Space Agency). The system is actually being tested to demonstrate its real radar capacities for space objects detection and tracking.

articleTitle: Method of fuzzy pattern recognition in one-demotion range profile recognition based on scatter central
abstract: Scatter central feature of high resolution range profile (HRRP) is sensitive to radar incident angles. So there are two problems that may influence the result of HRRP recognition, the recognition templates cannot be made full use of, and there is no reasonable order to arrange the feature vector. In this paper, a new method is proposed based on fuzzy information processing, and the training and recognition process is illuminated. Compared with other algorithms, the most important difference is that the dimension of the feature vector is no longer fixed. So the feature vector contains more target information and can be used more flexibly. At last, the feasibility of this algorithm is verified through experiment.

articleTitle: Radio individual identification via stable communication signals based on subordinate component analysis
abstract: In this paper, the wireless communication stable signal is decomposed into three components, i.e., communication waveforms, individual modulations and system noise. From the eigenvalue spectrum of the observed signal, it is found that the primary components, i.e., the several largest eigenvalues, correspond to the communication waveforms while those minimal components are caused by the noise. Meanwhile, the subordinate components can act as the features for individual identification. Accordingly, a novel method is proposed based on subordinate component analysis and real measuring data are provided to demonstrate its effectiveness.

articleTitle: Texture-based urban detection using contourlet coefficient on remote sensing imagery
abstract: This paper presents an original urban detection on remote sensing images, which is based on efficient textural features extracted from contourlet transform domain. Since cities and towns are consisted of various objects, which have great differences in scale, directivity and texture characteristics, it is adaptive for contourlet transform to detecting urbans result from its discrete-domain multi-resolution and multi-direction expansion using nonseparable filter banks. Therefore, construction of contourlet coefficients can capture the intrinsic geometrical structure that is the key in visual information. On the other hand, we employ robust texture features in contourlet domain for recognizing urban regions from other land type by LS-SVM classifier. The performance of the proposed approach was validated by experiments carried on a data set of large images consisting of heavily negative samples.

articleTitle: Measurement estimation in forward scatter radar with a planar array
abstract: A technique is presented for estimating the primary measurements of forward scatter radar with a planar array. The space-time processing based on three-dimensional discrete Fourier transform is employed and the computation is reduced without loss of accuracy. By analyzing the Cramer-Rao lower bound, the performance of the given approach is shown. Meanwhile, the effect of the target's complex scatter coefficient to the Doppler measurement is noticed. Numerical simulation presents an estimation of primary measurements with good accuracy.

articleTitle: The distinguishable ellipse resolution analysis and co-optimization in squinted SARs
abstract: The squinted SAR (Synthetic Aperture Radar, SAR) exhibits the feature of non-uniform resolution in different directions. The resolution analysis based on distinguishable ellipse is proposed, the expression of which on the slant and ground plane is derived respectively by GAF (generalized ambiguity function, GAF). The parameters sensitivity is analyzed and the joint optimization criterion of SAR geometry for maximizing the resolving performance is presented. This method conquers the conventional restrictions by uniform un-coupling resolutions in each direction. A series of simulation results demonstrate that this method is adaptive to the conditions of different geometries and system parameters. The effectiveness of joint optimization design is verified, which can provide a theoretical basis for the design of system parameters and geometry configuration in squinted SARs.

articleTitle: Synthetic aperture radar operation mode recognition based on time-frequency analysis
abstract: Recognition of Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) operation mode plays an important role in SAR countermeasure, and possesses quite significant sense in both theory and applications. Characteristics of three different SAR operation modes are analyzed in detail and the Doppler history of SAR signal is concerned. An algorithm by extracting Doppler Centroid with time frequency distribution (TFD) is proposed to retrieve SAR operation mode. Simulations are executed and all results have been proved that, the algorithm is correct and effective. It provides an effective way to SAR operation mode recognition.

articleTitle: Comparison between SRTM-C DEM and ICESat elevation data in the arid Kufrah area
abstract: Radar has the capability of penetration into low-loss dry sand down to bedrock beneath. This suggests the possibility of 3D bedrock topography retrieval using SAR interferometry beneath dry sand. The influence of different penetration depths on the InSAR DEM generation is analysed initially based on a two-layer sand model. Meanwhile, ICESat elevation data and the SRTM-C DEM associated with a SRTM-C amplitude image are employed to make a comparison to reveal the penetration of C-band radar wave in the Libyan Kufrah desert region. On the basis of the analysis and the comparison, it is inferred that the SRTM-C DEM is mostly affected by the subsurface height.

articleTitle: Circular SAR optimization imaging method about buildings based on the principle of high SNR
abstract: CSAR (Circular SAR) achieves 360° observation on the target by circular moving and beam controlling of platform, obtaining all-round scattering information and having significant advantages in the aspect of building geometric feature description. According to the buildings scattering feature and shape feature, this paper puts forward a CSAR optimization imaging method about buildings based on the principle of high SNR. The method establishes the electromagnetic scattering model of buildings to simulate the CSAR echo and image by using FEKO, a software of electromagnetic simulation. Furthermore, comparing and analysing the imaging result with the case of scattering isotropic, we conclude the best range of azimuth angle of coherent accumulation when the building CSAR imaging has fine SNR. Due to the scattering direction of buildings is unknown in the actual scene, CSAR 360° echo is divided into a plurality of sub apertures, overlapping each other in small angle. Finally, imaging for every sub aperture, all-round composite image is obtained by extracting the maximize value of each pixel in every sub aperture images. Validating by P band CSAR data processing, the proposed CSAR imaging method is superior to the traditional full coherent accumulation CSAR imaging method, which can realize high SNR imaging of buildings.

articleTitle: Strategy of spectrum reconstruction in stepped-frequency SAR imaging
abstract: High range resolution of synthetic aperture radar (SAR) can be obtained by using the stepped-frequency technique, but it is still a problem how spectrum reconstruction methods can be combined correctly and effectively with SAR imaging algorithms. This paper analyzes the feasibilities of all the potential combinations between spectrum reconstruction methods and SAR imaging algorithms, and the optimal combinations are proposed. The simulation results verify the analysis in this paper.

articleTitle: Double channels DDC to multi-frequency satellite navigation signals
abstract: Direct RF sampling technique is a method to receive navigation signals directly, after that we pass the signals after A/D to the down conversion system, and then get the baseband signals. However, the satellite navigation signal frequency is quite high, the sampling frequency required is also high, and this will bring a series of problems to us, so we should pass the sampled signals through a series of operations such as filtering, mixing and extraction, in order to get the baseband signals which are convenient for us to further processing. In this paper, we present a new digital down conversion (DDC) which has double channels and based on RF sampling.

articleTitle: An improved tracking algorithm of maneuvering targets based on CSHGMM
abstract: This paper considers the decline problem of tracking accuracy caused by acceleration estimation inaccuracy in hybrid grid multiple model (HGMM) algorithm. A new improved tracking algorithm of maneuvering targets based on CSHGMM is proposed. Grid partition is performed by estimation of the acceleration mean in current statistic (CS) model, where a fading factor is adopted to improve tracking accuracy by adjusting the gain matrix under the condition of the abrupt change of acceleration. Then possible model sets of the target are generated online, and interactive multiple model algorithm is adopted to estimate the target state. The proposed algorithm performance is tested and compared in general and strong maneuvering scenarios, and simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm not only improves the accuracy for maneuvering target tracking, but also can be applied to most of the tracking scenarios.

articleTitle: An ISAR imaging algorithm for micro-motion targets with sparse aperture
abstract: Micro-Doppler (m-D) effect is regarded as a unique signature for the targets with micro-motion parts. It may contaminate the target's inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) image and make the focused target hard to recognize. Meanwhile, multiple function radar system inevitably brings sparse apertures in practice due to its limited resources. In this paper, a method aiming at the ISAR imaging for micro-motion targets with sparse aperture is proposed. Based on an improved Hough transform and the orthogonal matching pursuit algorithm, the proposed method could not only extract the information of micro-motion parts, but also reconstruct the ISAR images for the main body targets. The simulation results of a target model with micro-motion parts illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Multitarget tracking algorithm based on LDL decomposition
abstract: Random target number, heavy clutter, and heavy target density make difficult for multiple targets tracking. Gaussian mixture Cardinalized probability hypothesis density (GMCPHD) filter based on theory of finite set statistics can perform this tracking task while with complex computation. It is well known that the computation of square-root Kalman filter based on LDL decomposition is about the half of the one in extend Kalman filter (EKF). Hence, this paper design a multitarget tracking algorithm based on LDL decomposition which called LDL-GM-CPHD filter. Numerical example is given in this manuscript and the simulation results reveal that LDL-GM-CPHD filter can save about 30% time resource with similar tracking performance.

Author Keywords: Gaussian mixture Cardinalized probability hypothesis density (GM-CPHD) filter

articleTitle: A new interacting multiple model algorithm for maneuvering target tracking based on adaptive transition probability updating
abstract: A new interacting multiple model (IMM) algorithm for maneuver target tracking is proposed in this paper. An adaptive updating method of the model transition probability is developed based on Bayes Theorem. Reinitialization strategies of the transition probabilities are design for two special cases. Then the updated transition probabilities are used to fulfill the interaction of the models. The proposed algorithm is of lower computational burden. Numerical simulations for both filtering and smoothing are given to demonstrate estimation performance.

articleTitle: Virtual multi-views method for through-wall radar imaging based on Green function
abstract: In this paper we utilize the multipath return to improve the image resolution and the signal-to-clutter ratio (SCR). Based on the modified indoor radio propagation model and the multipath scattering model, a method for localizing the focused multipath ghost is provided, then an algorithm combined the through-wall Green function with Back Propagation (BP) algorithm for association and mapping the multipath ghosts to their genuine targets is presented. The analysis is demonstrated with simulated data generated by GPRMAX.

articleTitle: Pulse repetition frequency design for geosynchronous SAR in ellipcial orbit
abstract: Elliptical orbit and squint mode are widely used in the system design of geosynchronous synthetics aperture radar (GEO SAR) to improve the coverage performance. In this paper, the effects of orbit height variation and squint mode to pulse repetition frequency (PRF) design are analyzed. The orbit height variation causes the variation of nadir interference and beam illumination region, and squint mode produces large range cell migration (RCM). These can induce invalidations of the designed PRF. Based on this, the constraints of nadir interference and transmit interference are updated for GEO SAR, and the effective time for the designed PRF is derived. PRF number required for imaging in one orbital period is analyzed.

articleTitle: Polarimetric SAR image change detection based on three-component decomposition
abstract: On the basis of the polarimetric distance measurement, this paper presents an improved method of change detection through a complete model-based decomposition of the polarimetric synthetic aperture radar (POLSAR) covariance/coherency matrix data. Due to the capability of accurately characterizing the structural features for polarization decomposition, the proposed method first utilizes the Freeman-Durden decomposition (FDD) to extract the polarization scattering characteristics of different land objects. Then, the refined Lee filter is applied to reduce the speckle noise. Finally, an improved distance measurement of change detection for multi-temporal POLSAR data is proposed. ALOS PALSAR polarimetric data from October 08, 2008 and November 23, 2008 covering agricultural fields near north Toronto, Canada are used. The experiments demonstrate that the proposed method can distinguish the changes effectively and preferably compared with the conventional method based on the distance measurement.

articleTitle: A fast stepped-frequency chirp radar imaging method based on NuFFT
abstract: A fast matched-filtering imaging method is presented based on non-uniform fast Fourier transform (NuFFT) for stepped-frequency chirp radar imaging. Multiple point scatters are selected in the scene and SNR of them are calculated. Moreover, traditional imaging methods are analysed and compared with the method in the study. Imaging results show obvious advantages of the method. Computational complexity is also analysed. Finally, the simulation results are utilized to validate the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Analysis of transient scattering from a conductor coated by multilayer thin materials using time domain integral equation
abstract: This paper concentrates on an efficient marching-on-in-time (MOT)-based time domain integral equation (TDIE) method for the analysis of the transient electromagnetic scattering from perfect electrically conducting (PEC) coated by multilayer thin materials. Like its frequency domain counterpart, the proposed method can reduce the number of unknowns significantly while reasonable accuracy can be achieved. Numerical example is presented to demonstrate the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed method.

Author Keywords: conductor coated by multilayer thin materials

articleTitle: Design of C/Ka dual-band wideband and wide-angle scanning multifunction phased array
abstract: The multifunction phased array is at present the best choice for the new generation air-to-air missile guidance system. The use of a phased array allows to have the benefits of the electronic scanning. In this paper, a novel dual-band phased array in the C/Ka-bands with wideband and wide-angle scanning capability is designed in the radar seeker application. A new tapered slot antenna (TSA) is used for the array design. The novel antenna is optimized by wizardly grooves and notches on the patch for wideband and wide-angle radiation. Simulation results show that the Voltage Standing Wave Ratio (VSWR) of the antennas are below 1.6 at the two frequency bands, and wide-angle scanning up to a maximum of 60° can be achieved in this dual-band phased array.

articleTitle: Target detection and localization using multi-frame information for noncoherent MIMO radar
abstract: This paper considers the target detection and localization via jointly processing multi-frame information, attainable by the use of multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar with widely separated antennas. By incorporating the target dynamic model, the problem can be formulated and solved in the framework of maximum a posteriori probability (MAP) criterion. However, the analytical solution of the posteriori probability density is usually intractable. A grid based search method is needed to achieve a computationally tractable approximation. For most realistic problems, directly performing exhaustive search is computationally prohibited due to the high dimensionality of state space. Therefore we resort to dynamic programming algorithm as a fast implementation to reduce the calculation burden. Owing to the utilization of multi-frame information of targets, the proposed algorithm can achieve better detection performance and higher localization accuracy, particularly when the target signal-to-noise ratio is low. Finally, numerical examples are used to demonstrate the efficiency of the proposed algorithm comparing with the localization method only using single-frame information.

articleTitle: Motion estimation of micro-motion targets with translational motion
abstract: This paper models the echo returned from a micro-motion target with translational motion as the hybrid sinusoidal frequency-modulated and polynomial-phase signal (SinFM-PPS). We decouple the SinFM component from the PPS one, relying on the properties of the multi-lag high-order ambiguity function (ml-HAF), then employ the time-frequency distribution(TFD)-Hough transform to get robust estimation of the parameters of the two signal components. The simulation results show the validity of our proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Estimation and removal of multiple scattering contributions to HF surface wave radar echoes
abstract: Existing techniques for remote sensing of ocean surface conditions by HFSWR are predicated on the assumption that the Doppler spectrum recorded at a given time delay and direction of arrival can be associated with the ground range and bearing corresponding to great circle propagation over a smooth surface. In this paper we investigate the consequences of the spatio-temporal modulation accumulated by the radar signal during its transit across the intervening rough ocean surface. Specifically, we explore the dependence of the measured spectrum on the apparent range, and examine factors which may be exploited to develop an inversion scheme for multiply-scattered signals.

articleTitle: An approach of gross error elimination in GNSS receiver hot start
abstract: With the rapid development of the GNSS receiver's performance, almost all the commercial receivers have the ability of hot start. The main algorithm of fast positioning is how to get the position before frame synchronization when hot start. Because of the incomplete information of the pseudorange calculation before frame synchronization, the pseudorange is calculated by its estimation of integer millisecond part and inside millisecond part. If the estimation is wrong, the position error will be huge because of the huge pseudorange error, and it need to be researched and improved further. Firstly, the principle of fast positioning when hot start is introduced, the estimation and combination of pseudorange before frame synchronization and the correction of the position of satellite because of the unknown of the send time are derived in detail. The influence of the shift of general position and coarse receiver time error to fast positioning is discussed, the result shows the accuracy of fast positioning when the shifting is not abnormal and original least squares are nearly the same. When the pseudorange combination is just in the middle of a millisecond, a little shift of general position and coarse receiver time error will lead to a huge estimation error in pseudorange. For the gross error coming from the misestimating of the pseudorange, robust least squares are proposed to correct the gross error, the result of the simulation shows it's an effective way to correct the gross error.

articleTitle: Synthesis of sparse concentric ring antenna arrays by convex optimization
abstract: An effective method for the synthesis of sparse concentric ring array with uniform amplitude is proposed. Based on the Bessel function properties of far field dictated by the circular array and the theory of Compressed Sensing, the synthesis can be formulated as a convex optimization problem with minimization of l1 norm. The radii and weights of the sparse concentric rings can be optimized simultaneously by sequential convex optimization method. The number of elements with uniform amplitude equally located on each ring is determined directly since it is proportional to the corresponding weight. The proposed method for concentric ring array optimization aims to achieve the desired power mask by adjusting the radii and the number of elements per ring. Moreover, the method is very easy to implement and has low computational burden. Numerical experiments are carried out to validate the flexibility and effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Road and vehicle detection in highway scene for automotive FMCW antenna array radar
abstract: This paper deals with the road and vehicle detection problem in highway scene for automotive radar which uses frequency-modulated continuous-wave (FMCW) signals and antenna array. Due to the automotive radar's low angle resolution, targets such as guardrails on road edge interfere with the vehicle detection and bring difficulties to the distance-velocity decoupling. We proposed an approach with Hough transformation and image matching for the road and vehicle detection. The interference of outroad targets is suppressed and the decoupling is achieved with low complexity. Specially, based on the road boundary model, the road boundary can be achieved by a curve Hough transform. Then, the on-road vehicles are detected and the distance-velocity decoupling can be solved by target region image matching with a total variation minimization method. Our new algorithm has a low computational complexity, and is validated by field experimental results.

articleTitle: Wind turbine clutter mitigation based on matching pursuits
abstract: Wind turbines could have a serious impact on Air Traffic Control (ATC) radar system because of the complex electromagnetic scattering properties. In this paper, matching pursuit technology is studied to mitigate the wind turbines interference. Due to the large amount of calculation in the conventional MP algorithm, rotation rate of wind turbine and radar azimuth are firstly estimated based on the priori information, then matching pursuit algorithm is applied to mitigate the wind turbine clutter. Effectiveness of the proposed method is verified via simulation experiments.

articleTitle: Sequential determination based multipath suppression algorithm for through wall imaging radar
abstract: In this paper, we consider the problem of the multiple targets imaging behind the walls with a through wall imaging radar, where a target image might overlap with the multipath ghosts introduced by some other targets. We propose a sequential determination based algorithm to delete the multipath ghosts while keeping the true target images when the overlapping occurred. Specifically, first, we develop a through wall imaging model by addressing on the first-order side wall multipath propagation. Second, we obtain the images of the true targets and possibly the multipath ghosts. Then, we exploit all the locations of these images to form a sequence and judge if they are the multipath ghosts or not in a sequential way. Finally, we delete the marked multipath ghost images. Some simulations are provided to evaluate the performance of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: A novel method of optimal multi-area search for phased array radar
abstract: With dynamical change of the environment, the optimal allocation of search resources is required for multi-area search of phased array radar. A parameter optimization model based on the weighted average discovering range of the penetration target is built in this paper. By joint search load allocation and search frame time adjustment optimal performance is achieved with initial search resources. Then three search load adjustment strategies named EAS(Equal Adjustment Strategy), LAS(Least-important Adjustment Strategy) and AAS(Adaptive Adjustment Strategy) are presented when search resources become limited. Simulation results prove the effectiveness of the optimal algorithm, and it's indicated that AAS provides the least performance loss compared to the other two strategies.

articleTitle: A high performance FFT processor based on conflict-free memory access
abstract: A new design method of FFT processor is proposed based on conflict-free memory access to satisfy the requirements for both high data throughout rate and low logic resource utilization. Aiming to realize a 1024/256 point compatible FFT processor with radix-4, decimation in time algorithm and block floating point arithmetic, four separate memory blocks are used to achieve conflict-free parallel data input and output for butterfly computation unit. Compared with some existing FFT processors, the design and verification results indicate that the proposed FFT processor has better real-time performance, low structure complexity and logic resource occupation.

articleTitle: Analysis of X-band polinsar coherence characteristics in forested areas
abstract: In this paper, the X-band coherence statistical characteristics related to the height of ambiguity and polarization of two typical forested areas is investigated, using X-band multibaseline polarimetric InSAR data acquired by an automobile-based InSAR system. Furthermore, according to the analysis of the coherence statistical characteristics of the experimental data, we propose an empirical model in relation to the height of ambiguity, polarization and forest height, which can be used as a reference for InSAR baseline configuration in forest mapping and forest height inversion based on multibaseline InSAR data.

articleTitle: Negative obstacle sensing based on real data of ultra-wideband SAR
abstract: It is a difficult task for an unmanned ground vehicle using regular sensor to sense obstacles in unstructured environments or out fields, especially on negative obstacle sensing. In this paper, we present an approach for negative obstacle sensing, based on ultra-wideband synthetic aperture radar (SAR) image characteristic of negative obstacle sensing. And real data on negative obstacle sensing is collected by ultra-wideband synthetic aperture radar (SAR). In all, we carried out three experiments by using three different frequency band antennas, and experimental results show that ultra-wideband synthetic aperture radar (SAR) can display edge information of negative obstacle in synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images.

articleTitle: Radar maneuvering target detection based on scaling processing and Radon-Fourier transform
abstract: A novel long-time coherent integration method, i.e., scaling processing and Radon-Fourier transform (SPRFT), is proposed to detect the low-observable manuevering target, which can compensate the range and Doppler migrations simultaneously. The target signal can be well accumulated as an obvious peak in the centroid frequency-chirp rate (CFCR) domain by simple FT calculations. It is shown that proposed SPRFT is a generalized form of RFT and Lv's distribution (LVD), which includes the long-time instantaneous autocorrelation function, scaling process, and RFT calculation. Experiments using real radar data indicate that the SPRFT can achieve better integration and detection performance than FRFT, RFT, and LVD with high efficiency.

articleTitle: A novel recognition method for hybrid modulation radar signals
abstract: This paper proposes a method to identify the hybrid modulation signals. Firstly, the method utilizes instantaneous frequency (IF) of signals combined with histogram to classify conventional signals and hybrid modulation signals. Then an improved signal segmentation method is used to resolve the hybrid modulation signals to conventional signals. Experimental results show that the proposed method can identify seven kinds of typical radar signals, and achieve 94% recognition accuracy when SNR is 3dB.

articleTitle: A sparse constraint beamformer based MVPS using polarization sensitive array
abstract: In this paper, we propose a new beamformer using a polarization sensitive array (PSA), which is based on minimum variance polarization sensitive (MVPS) and sparse constraint. The proposed adaptive beamformer shows superiority to the MVPS beamformer, and the performance of the proposed beamformer is demonstrated through computer simulations, both in no-mismatch and mismatch situations.

articleTitle: Modified polar format algorithm for ISAR imaging
abstract: Migration through resolution cells (MTRC) happened in large rotation angle inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) imaging can be effectively eliminated by Polar Format Algorithm (PFA) under the far-field condition. However, traditional PFA is sensitive to range error, so it is difficult to be implemented into engineering. Aimed at this problem, a modified polar format algorithm for ISAR imaging is proposed in this paper. Firstly, echo data is compressed to one-dimensional (1-D) range profiles, envelope alignment and phase autofocus processing are applied to compensate the translational motion, and the target motion model is converted into a turntable model. Next, the rotation center of the target should be obtained, and its envelope would be compensated to range zero. Then, two 1-D interpolation operations are applied to process data from polar sector support region to Cartesian rectangular grid. Finally, Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) operations are carried out to get well focused the ISAR image. The new method needs no range information, and therefore the image quality is not affected by the range errors. Theoretical analysis and simulation results verified the effectiveness of the algorithm proposed in this paper.

articleTitle: Lower ionosphere nonlinearity study on high frequency time service signal in China
abstract: The multiple non-linear interaction theory model of high-frequency (HF) electromagnetic wave and Schumann Resonance (SR) is constructed on the basis of ionosphere cross modulation. The global SR distribution, particularly the phase variation effect on the modulation depth of HF waves and SR, is investigated. Results show that modulation depth is not proportional to the interaction distance under the condition of multiple interactions. A new SR observation method is proposed, and the observatory system is designed on the basis of theoretical research. China short-wave time service signal called BPM is received and demodulated. The first four spectral peaks of SR are obtained at 7.8, 14, 20 and 26Hz. The multiple non-linear interaction theory model of HF electromagnetic wave and SR is proven by the experiment. Signal analysis comparison is conducted and recommendations for future work are proposed.

articleTitle: Precession feature analysis of ballistic targets by FMCW-ISAR
abstract: Precession is a typical kind of micro-motion of space targets such as ballistic targets. It has considerable significance to analyze the precession feature of ballistic targets in space target recognition and classification applications. A new idea using FMCW-ISAR (frequency modulation continuous wave-inverse synthetic aperture radar) system to extract micromotion features is presented in this paper, which opens up a new road for precession feature analysis. FMCW-ISAR system is consecutively transmitting and receiving signals, which gives it an advantage over traditional pulse radar systems on precession parameter estimation, especially in the case of high precession angular velocity. In this paper, a cone-shaped ballistic target model is set up, and theoretical analysis for basic precession feature extraction using a FMCW-ISAR system is discussed for the first time. The preliminary simulation results validate the theoretical analysis conclusions.

articleTitle: Implementation on FPGA for CORDIC-based computation of arcsine and arccosine
abstract: This paper concentrates on the hardware implementation of CORDIC algorithm for computing inverse trigonometric functions like arcsine and arccosine. We improve the existing algorithm by changing the initial rotating vector of the iterations and modifying the judging condition of rotation direction. Due to the improvement, two iterations are saved and the drawback of the previous algorithm is corrected.
