In contrasting with the previous implementation, the improved algorithm consumes less hardware resources and its computing results are more accuracy.

articleTitle: Methods to improve system verification efficiency in FPGA-based spaceborne SAR image processing system
abstract: With the rapid development of satellite-based signal processing technologies comes the widespread deployment of SAR image processing systems in spaceborne applications, many of which are implemented as FPGAbased systems thanks to the introduction of modern programmable devices with high capacity and complexity. However, as raw data of SAR satellites grow in size and bandwidth the effective implementation and especially the efficient system verification are emerging as the bottleneck in the development of FPGA-based SAR image processing systems. This paper proposes methods in the verification phase of FPGA-based SAR processing system development which on one hand increases the verification speed during simulations and on the other addresses the hardware/Matlab mismatch issue through comparison of floating point numbers on grounds of error analysis from a mathematical approach. Actual development process indicate that the proposed methods guarantee quick design convergence, and test results on real hardware confirm that the SAR image processing system offers acceptable quality of image output.

articleTitle: Comparison of detectability of radar waveforms using a digital channelized receiver
abstract: The detectability of instantaneously narrowband and wideband radar waveforms in a digital channelized receiver is studied in this work. The waveforms include monotone, linear frequency modulation (LFM), phase coded (PC), frequency coded (FC) and orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM). Simulation results indicate that low probability of intercept (LPI) performance of these waveforms depends on bandwidth, especially instantaneous bandwidth, and the distribution of signal power over the whole bandwidth. An ideal LPI waveform should have broad instantaneous bandwidth and make the waveform energy uniformly spread over the occupied band. Among these waveforms, it is demonstrated that PC and OFDM signals have the lowest detection probabilities in a channelized receiver.

articleTitle: Research on simultaneous polarimetric measurement based on PN-NLFM signals
abstract: Simultaneous polarimetric radar transmits a pair of orthogonal signals through a pair of orthogonal polarization channels. The signals transmitted must both have good auto-correlation and cross-correlation characteristics. In this paper, a novel simultaneous polarimetric measurement technique based on positive and negative NLFM (PN-NLFM) signals is proposed. According to the simultaneous polarimetric waveform design criteria proposed in this paper, the PN-LFM, I-OFDM and PN-NLFM signals are compared in performance of range resolution and polarization isolation. The simulation results show that PN-NLFM signals can achieve better range resolution and less mainlobe width than PN-LFM. The polarization isolation level of PN-NLFM signals is about 40 dB. Though polarization isolation is 10 dB less than I-OFDM, PN-NLFM signals perform better for targets which are sensitive to frequency. Thus PN-NLFM signals are a proper waveform for simultaneous polarimetric radar.

articleTitle: A fast 2D-ESPRIT super-resolution imaging algorithm for linear array SAR
abstract: Linear array SAR can realize accurate 3D imaging and has many civilian and military uses. High imaging resolution is its most important parameter, but is limited by the realistic conditions such as the length of the fuselage and wings. In this work, a fast 2D-ESPRIT super-resolution imaging algorithm is proposed which can synchronously achieve super-resolutions in cross-track and along-track directions. Then, a modified matching method based on region growing algorithm is utilized, which obviously decreases calculating time. Simulation results show its validity.

Author Keywords: Estimation of signal parameters by rotational invariance technique (ESPRIT) algorithm

articleTitle: NUFFT-based parameter estimation algorithm for ISAR imaging of targets with complex motion
abstract: For inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) imaging of targets with complex motions, the received signals have to be modeled as multi-component cubic phase signals (CPSs) after motion compensation. The innovation of this paper includes the introduction of the nonuniform fast Fourier transform (NUFFT) algorithm to obtain high-quality ISAR images rapidly. Because of the application of the NUFFT and the SCFT via chirp-z transform (CZT) with respect to the lag-time axis and time axis, respectively, the proposed algorithm can achieve a compromise between performance and low computational complexity in estimating the parameters. Both the theoretical analysis and the simulation examples demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Fast factorized back projection algorithm for spotlight bistatic forward-looking low frequency UWB SAR
abstract: Spotlight bistatic forward-looking synthetic aperture radar (BFSAR) is a valid tool in the precise surveillance and attacking mission. Because the low frequency ultrawideband (UWB) spotlight BFSAR has the complicated range-azimuth coupling, diverse imaging geometry, and long synthetic aperture, etc., the application of frequency-domain algorithms is limited. In this paper, an extended fast factorized back-projection (FFBP) algorithm is presented to focus the low frequency UWB spotlight BFSAR data. First, the imaging geometry and signal model are established, and the idea of implementation of continuous surveillance and moving target indication (MTI) is presented. Then, the phase error of the FFBP algorithm for processing the spotlight BFSAR data is analyzed, and the implementation of the proposed FFBP algorithm is given. Finally, the simulation experiment is carried out to prove the validity of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Bistatic 3D interferometric ISAR phase unwrapping
abstract: Interferometric ISAR is a promising technique which uses phase difference between ISAR images generated by multiple sensors to obtain the height information and the effective rotational motion of the target with respect to radar. However, the phase of the interferogram must be unwrapped to remove the modulo-ambiguity before estimating the height and rotation of the target. In the conventional phase unwrapping operation, it is assumed that the true (unwrapped) phase difference between adjacent pixels is beyond the range [-π,π]. In the ISAR applications, the rapid changes in the true intrinsic phase will violate this assumption. Inconsistencies can lead to phase unwrapping errors. In this paper, a phase unwrapping method is developed to solve this problem. Simulations have been carried out to verify the effectiveness of our method.

articleTitle: Impulse radio UWB radar pulse detector
abstract: A UWB radar pulse detector concept was evaluated in simulation, and was then tested with an in-house setup for experimental UWB link. The simulations were across 3.1-10.6 GHz, the working prototypes (pulse generator, directional coupler, Vivaldi antenna, LNA, pulse detector) that composed the proof of concept were referenced and the UWB link operated across 2.8-5.2GHz, showing that the use of COTS hardware enables the low cost and low complexity RF design for UWB applications with respectable performances.

articleTitle: A new method to correct background ionospheric phase distortion in GEO SAR
abstract: The background ionosphere has a great influence on the phase of echoes in geosynchronous synthetic aperture radar (GEO SAR) due to the long integration time. This paper presents a new method to correct background ionospheric phase distortion in GEO SAR, which directly estimates of background ionosphere from optimize the coherent addition value along the range equation using the range compressed data. In addition, the optimization problem is solved by the particle swarm optimization (PSO) with an overall accuracy and a higher converging speed. Finally, the simulation results show this method can estimate the background ionosphere effectively and the phase distortion can be corrected on GEO SAR.

articleTitle: An improved track-before-detect strategy for STAP radars
abstract: The knowledge of the operating environment (whether scan-to-scan varying or stationary) has a significant impact on the performance of the original adaptive track-before-detect (TBD) strategy for space-time adaptive processing (STAP) radars. If the knowledge assumption is not met, the performance degrades dramatically due to the mismatch between the true covariance matrix and the estimated one. To deal with this problem, an improved adaptive TBD strategy is proposed in this paper, which reduces the impact of data contaminated by signal or interferer components on the estimation of covariance matrix and thus improves the performance. Computational complexity and performance of the proposed adaptive TBD strategy are analyzed and compared with the original adaptive TBD strategy.

articleTitle: Ground moving target detection using monopulse-SAR
abstract: Equipped with a monopulse antenna, airborne synthetic aperture radar (SAR) gains the ability to detect the ground slowly moving targets. This paper focuses on the constant false alarm rate (CFAR) detection of moving targets for monopulse-SAR. The statistics of complex monopulse ratio (CMR), under complex Gaussian clutter-plus-noise background, is examined in detail when target present or absent. Based on that, a two-step CFAR detector with the probability of false alarm (PFA) given in a closed-form expression for moving target detection is presented and extended to a so called multi-complex monopulse diagram (CMD) form to further improve the final detection performance. Experimental results obtained from two groups of measured dataset are presented to examine the detection performance and validate the theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: High Doppler tolerance waveform design algorithm based on ambiguity function
abstract: Waveform design algorithm based on ambiguity function is researched. To the problem of poor delay-Doppler performance, firstly construct the desired ambiguity function which satisfy delay-Doppler performance and low autocorrelation, secondly diagonal loading approach has been used to make its correlation matrix positive definite. The difference between the designed ambiguity function and the desired one are used as a criterion, the waveform design problem is transform to optimization problem, the unit-modulus sequences is got by Cyclic Algorithm. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm had better delay-Doppler performance and lower two dimension sidelobe level with weak loss in zero-Doppler cut sidelobe level, besides this algorithm with rapid convergence rate.

articleTitle: A novel space target location method for spaceborne radar
abstract: Combined with the space target observation radar application requirements, related issues of spaceborne MMW (MilliMeter Wave) InISAR (Interferometric Inverse Synthetic Aperture Radar) are researched. A proposed system contains an L-shaped orthogonal observation structure is designed and analyzed basing on a spaceborne platform. The location of a space target can be acquired using imaging and interferometry, and the interferometric phase wrapping is solved by sub-band dual frequency conjugated processing (DFCP). The two-stage space target location method and the spaceborne radar system are presented. Finally, a simulation is designed and proven to be a feasible solution by the simulation experiment which also indicated the direction of the following research work.

articleTitle: A digital FLL and its steady-state performance analysis in Z domain
abstract: The Digital Frequency-Locked-Loop (DFLL), which is obtained usually by mapping Analog Frequency-LockedLoop (AFLL) to digital domain, is different greatly in performance from the origin AFLL, especially when loop update interval is long. To analyse DFLL's stead-state working performance, all-phase mathematical model of a typical DFLL is established in Z domain. Analytical expressions of relation between stead-state tracking error and stability condition with loop parameters are derived. Via comparing the derived expressions of DFLL with expressions of AFLL existed in literature, several important conclusions about the difference between DFLL and AFLL are drawn. Simulation results verify the above theoretical results. The conclusion of this paper is feasible but not limited to 2-order and 3-order DFLL which are commonly used in nowadays high-dynamic receiver, the derived expressions can be used for performance evaluation, parameters optimization and loop design of DFLL.

articleTitle: Airplane Landing-Aid imaging radar system and experiment
abstract: Safe landing of the plane on time is of notable importance for airport, while the current landing system of civil airplanes mainly rely on the pilot's observation of runway and aviation skills, which is disturbed by the weather. This paper presents a Landing-Aid Radar system with dual-GPU processor to use different methods to process different types of data, providing an ameliorative method for improving the angular resolution of scanning radar image. Experimental results demonstrate the efficiency and validly of the proposed system of the guidance in blind landing for civil airplanes.

articleTitle: Accurate non-contact vibration amplitude retrieval using least squares estimation
abstract: An accurate non-contact amplitude retrieval of the periodic movement is proposed in this paper. Firstly, the backscattered signal of a vibrational target can be expanded as a series of harmonics whose amplitudes are determined by the vibration amplitude. Then, based on the least squares estimation, all the available harmonics are utilized to suppress the influence of the signal noise on the vibration measurement, so as to improve the accuracy of vibration amplitude retrieval. Finally, the Monte Carlo simulation is performed to validate the effectiveness in the case of low signal-to-noise ratio (-9dB). Accuracy of the new method in different cases of signal-to-noise ratio is also obtained. In addition, the real experimental data acquired by a 100GHz millimeter radar is used to test the performance of the proposed method, associated with a calibrator of vibration. In the experiment, a calibrator of vibration is 30m away from the radar. The results show the proposed method has better accuracy than the ones in the case of only one harmonic pair is used.

articleTitle: Study on model of ionosphere fine structure for cognitive radar
abstract: It is required for the Cognitive Over-the-Horizon-Radar (COTHR) to deepen the cognition of the ionosphere environment. The current model of the ionosphere structure cannot satisfy this requirement. In this paper, the dispersion effect is introduced into the ionosphere fine structure and the space-time-frequency fine structure model of the ionosphere is proposed. Simulation results testify the validity of the model.

articleTitle: Parameter estimation algorithm for maneuvering targets
abstract: A novel method for parameter estimation of maneuvering targets is proposed in this paper to eliminate the influence of spectrum spread on image focusing. In this method, the received signal in a range cell is modelled as a multicomponent linear frequency modulated (LFM) signal after range compression and motion compensation, and then a new transform, namely, Doppler Lv's transform (LVT) is applied on the azimuth signal to estimate the parameters. The proposed method is capable of obtaining the accurate parameter estimates efficiently in the low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) scenario with low computational burden and memory cost. Simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A new reconfigurable methodology to implement the shift-and-correlate (SAC) algorithm for real-time SAR autofocusing
abstract: Doppler Frequency Rate (FDR) is an essential parameter in the procedure of Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) processing. In this paper, we investigate an achievable autofocus algorithm, shift-and-correlate (SAC), and design the implementation of FDR estimation. The proposed method can dramatically improve the accuracy of imaging and reduce the time delay of the SAR imaging process. Depth-of-focus theory and linear fitting theory are discussed in this paper for decreasing the computation-consumption and the preserving precision. We verify the proposed method in a 16384*16384 SAR imaging process at 100 MHz system clock on a dedicated designed Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) tested. To testify the feasibility of the proposed method, we compared our run-out results with existing implementations using traditional DSP and MATLAB methods in terms of real-time performance and imaging quality.

articleTitle: Adaptive beamforming based on compressed sensing for HF sky-surface wave radar
abstract: The High Frequency (HF) hybrid sky-surface wave radar is a new system radar, based on sky-wave transmitting and surface-wave receiving. However, recently, with the rapid development of inshore tourism and digital device, the appropriate beaches for antennas distribution are lesser and lesser, electromagnetic environment is more and more complex. So it is imperative to find a new way for HF over the horizon (OTH) hybrid mode radar system. This paper introduces elementary composing and operating principle of this hybrid mode radar system and a new adaptive digital beamforming method of HF OTH hybrid mode radar system on the receiving radar station based on compressed sensing (CS) and variable diagonal loading (VDL) methods are proposed. Because of the spatial sparseness of receiving target signals, so fewer element can be adopted to sample receiving signals. And then, the target echo of the absent channels can be restored by the Subspace Pursuit (SP) method of CS theory. Then the new adaptive digital beamforming can use the restored echo signals. Finally, the result of numerical experiment demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed arithmetic.

articleTitle: Optimization on the ambiguity properties of MIMO radar
abstract: For shedding light on the properties of range-folding, Doppler-frequency aliasing, and clutter rejection in match filtering of the MIMO radar, which are not available in publications, the paper focuses on analyzing and optimizing the ambiguity properties of the MIMO radar including the unambiguous delay interval and Doppler interval, the unambiguous area and the sidelobe level in the unambiguous area. As a result, the unambiguous area of the MIMO radar in the delay-Doppler plane is optimized to be 1 (dimensionless), and the sidelobe level in the unambiguous area is optimized to equal the sidelobe level of the SIMO radar, thus the MIMO radar can match the SIMO radar in the performance of range-folding, Doppler-frequency aliasing, and clutter rejection in match filtering.

articleTitle: Subdomain clutter reduction method for imaging near surface target
abstract: Penetrating radar for detecting near surface target is a kind of radar which can be used to detect, discern and image the small targets buried in the shallow surface of nonmetallic medium. The main clutter of this radar mechanism is the reflection wave transmitted between radar antennas and the surface of the non-metallic medium. If it cannot be reduced, the image of the small targets will be submerged. This paper presents a clutter reduction method which bases on the idea of subdomain mean cancellation to suppress the reflection wave of non-uniform surface of the medium. Experimental results prove that subdomain mean cancellation method can effectively repress the reflection wave of the medium surface and significantly improve the quality of the image.

articleTitle: Antenna pattern synthesis with multiple discrete and continuous nulls
abstract: Antenna pattern synthesis with a set of prescribed discrete nulls can be formulated as a least squares problem where the modified weight is in the null space of the antenna response matrix of the null region and the modified pattern is closest to the quiescent pattern. The solution involves determining the null space using the singular value decomposition (SVD) of the antenna response matrix of the null region. Here we are concerned with an antenna pattern synthesis problem in forming multiple nulls that include those that are continuously specified across intervals of prescribed widths. A conventional approach may involve discretizing the continuous nulls over the constraint width. An exact approach involves a quasi-matrix formulation of the antenna response or forming the correlation matrix over the continuous intervals. This paper uses quasiand mixed-matrix techniques to obtain the minimal set of basis vectors that best define nulls that may be continuously specified across intervals of prescribed widths; it then presents an efficient practical implementation procedure for inserting single as well as multiple extended and/or discrete nulls.

articleTitle: 2D DOA estimator for coherently distributed sources based on fourth order cumulants
abstract: In this paper, a new method to estimate the nominal two-dimensional (2D) direction-of-arrivals (DOAs) of multiple coherently distributed (CD) sources using two uniform linear arrays (ULAs) is proposed. Because the fourth-order cumulants of Gaussian random processing is equal to zero, the proposed method firstly constructs three fourth-order cumulants matrices for Gaussian noise suppression, which can result in the improvement of the performance of DOA estimation. Then the rotational invariant structure is exploited among the three fourth-order cumulants matrices. Finally, the nominal DOAs of coherently distributed sources are obtained from the eigenvalues of the rotational invariant matrices without spectrum peak searching. Compared with some existing methods, the proposed method exhibit a better estimation performance for CD sources even at the conditions of low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), small number of snapshots or different angular spread degrees. Simulation results validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A novel self-adaptive density-based clustering algorithm for radar signal sorting
abstract: Radar signal sorting, which de-interleaves pulse sequences from different radar emitters, is one of the key techniques in Electronic Support Measures (ESM) system of modern warfare. As the electromagnetic environment in modern electronic wars is complex and dense, conventional multi-parameter de-interleaving techniques cannot achieve satisfactory accuracy. Although clustering algorithms have shown promising results in signal sorting, they all have their own weaknesses. In this paper, we propose a novel densitybased clustering algorithm targeting radar signal sorting problem. Our clustering algorithm determines the number of clusters and the density thresholds by the distribution of the data itself rather than depending on user experience as in K-Means or other existing density-based algorithms. Multiple density thresholds may be generated when necessary. We ran our algorithm on a set of simulation radar data. It outperforms DBSCAN-based signal sorting algorithm a lot in terms of accuracy, missing sorting rate and the error sorting in each set of parameters. In addition, it is observed that our algorithm is insensitive to the parameters, ratio factor, uniformity, and quantile. Thus, our proposed self-adaptive density-based clustering algorithm is promising in solving radar signal sorting problem in real electromagnetic environment.

articleTitle: An improved DEM reconstruction method based on shortest sub-interval in MF-InSAR
abstract: Interferometric synthetic aperture radar (InSAR) can realize the elevation extraction of the target. Through increasing the degree of freedom (DOF) during the topography calculation, multi-frequency InSAR technology can further achieve high-accuracy elevation reconstruction in steep terrain. Although the maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) method is widely used in the signal processing of multi-frequency InSAR, its performance can be influenced by phase noise. This paper proposes a creative algorithm which combines the maximum likelihood elevation estimation with the shortest sub-interval seeking operator (SSIS-MLE). It statistically averages the elevation estimation results of the MLE with class histogram, so that efficiently excludes the error estimation. Simulation results verify that this method not only maintains the high calculation efficiency of traditional MLE method, but also guarantees the high accuracy of elevation estimation.

articleTitle: A selection method of frequency combination in MF-INSAR system
abstract: As an extension of the Interferometric Synthetic aperture radar (InSAR), the multi-frequency InSAR can realize high-accuracy elevation extraction of the steep terrain. Though the maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) is widely used in the signal processing of multi-frequency InSAR, the performance of this method can be influenced by the selection of frequency combination. At the beginning, this paper analyses the elevation estimated effectiveness of different frequency combinations from the aspect of Cramer-Rao Lower Bound (CRLB). Then, it calculates the ambiguity cycle as a further filter for the optimal frequency combination. Finally, this paper discusses the adaptability to the phase noise with the help of Monte Carlo simulation strategy. In consideration of these three aspects, a selection method of frequency combination is proposed, and further simulation results are provided in quantity. Relevant researches can be used in the design of multi-frequency InSAR system.

articleTitle: Experimental results and analysis for GBSAR deformation measurement
abstract: In this paper, the methodology, which uses GBSAR system to monitor the micro deformation of the scenario, was presented both theoretically and experimentally. In the process, the persistent scatterer (PS) technology was utilized to obtain the deformation of the scene. Firstly, the full basic PS process chain for deformation generation is presented. Secondly, the ground-based SAR system and the data acquisition of geometry are described briefly. Furthermore, the theoretical developments are complemented with the process of real data which is acquired in the experiment. Finally, the comparison between experimental results and local measurements is discussed, which demonstrated the feasibility of our GBSAR system to obtain high-precision deformation.

articleTitle: Fast computation method for electromagnetic scattering characteristics of unmanned air vehicle
abstract: A new electromagnetic scatter modeling method of simulation with measurement date is presented in detail. Unmanned air vehicle(UAV) is tested in the anechoic chamber, inlet and tail nozzle special part scattering point is extracted; Simultaneity applied the high-frequency approximated method, reflection at conducting surfaces is computed by using physical optics approximation; diffraction at edges by using physical theory of diffraction, electromagnetic scattering characters of targets simulation combining with the measurement date is fast obtained. The calculated results are consistent with the result from measurement, which assure validity of the method, high effectivity and accuracy.

articleTitle: Design of an X-band dual circularly polarized offset reflector antenna
abstract: A design of compact X-band dual circularly-polarized offset reflector antenna is described for the radar satellite system. The antenna is composed of a metallic reflector and a horn feed. By introducing the septum polarizer in the horn feed, it makes a more compact size for reduced space. Meanwhile, it is easier for the horn feed to reach the far field boundary condition. The offset reflector has obtained the circularly polarized radiation pattern of above 30dB gain, which the side lobe is less than -24dB; The axial ratio of the direction of the maximum radiation is below 1dB. And the two ports isolation is under -20dB at the center of the frequency of 8GHz. This configuration meet the reliability and consistency requirements for the space.

articleTitle: Analysis of micro-Doppler features for walking person recognition
abstract: Micro-Doppler feature can provide rich information for motion target classification and recognition of radar. Feature selection is a key step in target recognition and it is a valuable work to analyze the recognition features and the influential factors on recognition accuracy. Four features extracted from foot component and torso component are selected to recognize one walking person and two walking persons based on micro-Doppler in this paper. The impact of time window length and signal-to-noise ratio on the recognition accuracy is analyzed. The contribution of single feature to recognition rate is researched too. The corresponding results of simulation are shown in the paper.

articleTitle: Waveform design and analysis for radar and communication integration system
abstract: Nowadays integration of electronic platforms has been a new research area, in which the radar and communication integration system is becoming a hot topic. Aiming to solve the incompatibility of signal design between the radar and communication applications, and followed by the principle of signal energy sharing, a radar and communication integration system based on random stepped frequency waveform is proposed. The transmission information is modulated on the carrier frequency, which accomplished the communication function without affecting the imaging radar performance. The radar imaging is mainly accomplished using Compressed Sensing theory. Simulations and analysis prove its feasibility.

articleTitle: Single layer dual-band reflectarray antenna with two independent radiation patterns
abstract: This paper present a design for X/Ku dual-band reflectarray antennas with single layer which has two independent radiation patterns for X and Ku bands. In the design, a novel dual resonance structure has been used as the unit cell for both X and Ku band to achieve dual-band performance with a new approach. A 10×10 center-fed reflectarray operating at 9 GHz and 13.5 GHz with scattering angles of 12° and -30° respectively, is designed and the simulated results are presented to validate the approach.

articleTitle: Frequency estimation of cyclic spectrum carrier based on compressive sampling of BPSK signal
abstract: Binary phase shift keying (BPSK) signal is very important in modern digital communication, and its parameter estimation is of great significance to demodulation. It is well known that signal cycle spectrum which is robust to noise and the signal parameters are closely related, but it needs high speed sampling for broadband signal and puts forward high requirements for hardware. Compressive sensing is an academic hotspot which emerged in recent years, we reconstruct cyclic spectrum based on compressive sensing, and low sampling rate of recovery will play an important role in reducing the amount of calculations.

articleTitle: 2 × 2 Hybrid beamforming MIMO system for millimeter wave communication
abstract: The increase in growing traffic explosion in wireless communication system has recently drawn great attention to the large amount of underutilized spectrum is millimetre wave (mmWave) communication system as a potential candidate. Beamforming (BF) is an efficient technique to increase the capacity of the wireless communication systems. We proposed an efficient and less complex novel hybrid beamforming technique to maximize the channel capacity for large scale antenna system. A large number of transmit and receive antennas are partitioned into two BF groups. The optimal BF vectors of the groups are found to maximize the channel capacity in a mmWave channel. The algorithm is based on calculating the transmit and receive BF vectors for the partitioned antennas group, which focused on optimizing the BF vectors alternatively at the transmitter and receiver. The algorithm aims at maximizing the product of the dominant singular values of the partitioned channel matrices, thus maximizing the determinant of the 2 × 2 large scale MIMO system and eventually results in increase capacity of the system. The effectiveness of the beamforming algorithm is verified by extensive simulation results. Simulation results show considerable increase in the capacity of the system at high signal to noise ratio (SNR).

articleTitle: A new acceleration estimation method based on special FRFT in MIMO radar
abstract: Multiple input and multiple output (MIMO) radar can accumulate many more periods than Phased Array Radar. But when the target travels through the beam, the Doppler frequency motion may occur. So Doppler compensation must be done with more accurate acceleration estimation. The fractional Fourier transform (FRFT) methods in the references before are based on the analysis of global spectrum with fixed resolution and do not involve local detail spectrum. This paper puts forward using the united method of radical FRFT, Zoom-FRFT and single point FRFT for acceleration accurate estimation in MIMO radar.

Author Keywords: Multiple input and multiple output (MIMO) radar

articleTitle: Self-calibration for the multiple channel phase array system based on near-field weighting
abstract: Traditional in-field self-calibration techniques for some multiple channel systems, whose volume and weights are limited, are inefficient. A more simple calibration technique, employing only one assistant source in near-field and one transceiver channel, is investigated and it's unnecessary to conduct complex feed circuits behind the antennas. Furthermore, the calibration method in the principle of minimum channel errors with the near-field weighting (NFW) is proposed. It's a method in channel level for the compensation of errors between sub-arrays based on the proved fact that the channel errors have a stronger impact on the beam pattern than the random element errors. The channel errors could be obtained just by one time of measurement. A series of analysis and simulated results demonstrate that the proposed method is efficient in practice.

articleTitle: Comparison of several sparse reconstruction algorithms in SAR imaging
abstract: As the effective means for achieving sparse microwave imaging, sparse reconstruction algorithms (SRAs) can be generally classified into four main categories: greedy pursuits, l<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub>-norm minimization, nonconvex optimization and Bayesian framework. In this paper, we compare the performance of the typical SRAs in synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imaging. We consider four algorithms including the orthogonal matching pursuit (OMP), the iterative shrinkage-thresholding algorithm (IST), the iterative half thresholding algorithm (IHalfT) and the complex approximate message passing algorithm (CAMP), which are chosen from the aforementioned main categories respectively. In the light of theoretical analysis, we discuss the potential advantages of those algorithms applied to SAR, such as range-azimuth decoupling based 2-D reconstruction, adaptability to various modes of SAR imaging and parallel acceleration capability. On the basis of the results in the simulations and real data processing, the performance comparison of those algorithms is summarized in the end.

articleTitle: Water body extraction based on the LBV transformation analysis for China GF-1 multi-spectral images
abstract: For the surface water body extraction from China GF-1 satellite multi-spectral images, this paper proposes a algorithm based on the LBV transformation analysis method. The LBV transformed images can be used more effectively for the analysis of ground features than the original multispectral satellite images. So in the proposed method, the LBV transformation equations for GF-1 images are firstly discussed. Then, by analyzing gray level curves of six typical ground features in L(the general radiance level), B(the visible-infrared radiation) and V(the band radiance variation vector) images respectively, a decision criterion for extracting water body is obtain. And by this decision criterion the water bodies can be quickly and accurately extracted in the complex scenes. The experimental results show that this algorithm can effectively eliminate roads and the shadows of the buildings and cloud on the influence of the water body extraction and can exactly extract the small ponds, lakes and reservoirs. In addition, the proposed algorithm is simple, automatic and highly adaptable.

articleTitle: Iterative roubust sparse recoery method based on focuss for space-time adaptive processing
abstract: Conventional Space-time adaptive processing (STAP) requires large numbers of independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) training samples to ensure the clutter suppression performance, which is hard to be achieved in nonhomogeneous environment. In order to obtain improved clutter suppression with small training support, an iterative sparse recovery STAP algorithm is proposed in this paper. In the proposed method, the clutter spectrum sparse recovery and the calibration of space-time over-complete dictionary are implemented iteratively, modified focal underdetermined system solution (FOCUSS) with recursive calculation is used to alleviate the recovery error and reduce the computational cost, meanwhile the mismatch of space-time overcomplete dictionary is calibrated by minimized the cost function. Based on the simulated and the actual data, it is verified that the proposed method can not only converge with much smaller training samples compared with conventional STAP methods, but also provide improved performance compared with existing sparsity-based STAP methods.

articleTitle: The software pipeline realization of CFAR based on DSP
abstract: Constant False Alarm Rate (CFAR) algorithm is an important technology of radar system. It can provide optimal signal detection performance via maintaining a constant false alarm rate. However, the computational workload of estimating the clutter power of every data unit can be high. Thus, a software pipeline method for CFAR on the Digital Signal Processor(DSP) of TI's latest series C6000 family is proposed in this paper. Compared with non-optimized CFAR algorithm, software pipeline operation can achieve better performance and 41x improvement on instruction cycle.

articleTitle: Impact of T/R module performance on tradeoff design of airborne AESA radar
abstract: Transmit/Receive (T/R) modules are key components in Active Electronically Scanned Array (AESA) for advanced airborne radar, and their performance affects the capability of airborne AESA radar in several aspects. In this paper, a procedure is proposed with the tradeoff design of an AESA radar between the power-aperture product (PAP) and the peak-to-side lobe ratio (PSLR) of its antenna. While the PAP decides the maximum detection range, the PSLR is desired for low probability of intercept (LPI) radars as well as for alleviating clutter interference. The analysis results indicate that both high PAP and PSLR can not be achieved simultaneously based on the state-of-art performance of Ku-band T/R modules.

articleTitle: Effect evaluation for SAR suppression jamming based on edge strength image
abstract: Scientific effect evaluation plays an important role in SAR suppression jamming. However, experiment results show that, for the traditional assessment method based on correlation coefficient, the evaluation indexes are usually inconsistent with the feeling of the human eyes. In order to cope with this problem, a new evaluation method is proposed in this paper. In the method, two edge strength images are firstly obtained by apply ROEWA (ratio of exponentially weighted averages) operator in both SAR images before and after jamming. After that, a new evaluation index is achieved by computing the correlation of the two edge strength images. Experiment results show that, compared with the traditional evaluation methods, the new evaluation indexes is more consistent with the subjective feeling of the human eyes.

articleTitle: A histogram based method for micro-Doppler interference removal
abstract: The micro-Doppler interference generated by mechanical vibration or rotation of a target or its parts may cause the degeneration of radar images. Inspired by the observation that the frequency of occurrence of the rigid-body components is higher than that of the micro-Doppler interference at each frequency bin in time-frequency domain, a method based on histogram analysis is proposed for micro-Doppler interference removal. Compared to the recently developed L-statistics-based method, the proposed method preserves more uncontaminated data corresponding to the rigid-body components. Experimental results show that the radar image reconstructed by the proposed method has better quality than that provided by the L-statistics-based method.

articleTitle: Compressive sensing algorithm for downward-looking sparse array 3-D SAR imaging
abstract: Sparse array can avoid unwanted grating lobes and take full advantage of the wingspan space, which is widely applied in downward-looking 3-D SAR. In the paper, a 3D imaging strategy based on compressive sensing theory is proposed for downward-looking sparse array SAR imaging, which can improve the performance in cross-track direction. T/R sparse array and MIMO sparse array, as the representative distributions of the sparse array, are discussed in the paper. Compared with T/R sparse array, MIMO sparse array can achieve high imaging performance with less real antenna elements. Simulation results indicate that the proposed algorithm can provide high quality imagery compared to the conventional method.

articleTitle: Range side-lobe suppression method via CMR for pulse compression LPI waveform
abstract: Design of low probability of intercept (LPI) signal waveform is an important issue in design of LPI radar systems. Pulse compression waveforms having large time-bandwidth product are a kind of radar signals with good Radio Frequency (RF) stealth performance, and many pulse compression waveforms are investigated to reducing the radio frequency signals being intercepted, such as frequency hop code, phase code and etc. However, undesirable range sidelobes of these pulse compression waveforms generated by matched filter may mask small nearby targets. A sidelobe suppression algorithm by repairing Covariance Matrix for pulse compression LPI waveforms is presented in this paper, and the processing results of frequency hop codes illustrate that the high range sidelobes are successfully suppressed.

articleTitle: Random carrier-frequency Radon-Fourier transform for radar target detection
abstract: Radon-Fourier transform (RFT) realizes the long-time coherent integration to detect weak targets. However, because of discrete pulse sampling, finite range resolution, and limited integration time, the “blind-speed side lobes (BSSL)” of RFT may inevitably appear in real application. This paper proposes Random Carrier-Frequency Radon-Fourier transform (RCFRFT). It is a good solution for low SNR target detection and parameters estimation under Doppler ambiguity of long-range weak targets. Both theoretical analysis and simulation results show that RCF-RFT can be used to suppress BSSL of RFT. Also, it is shown that RCF-RFT significantly improves the detection and measurement ability of the radar.

articleTitle: Design of a configurable fixed-point FFT processor
abstract: In this paper, we focus on the widely-used radix-2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> Decimation-In-Frequency (DIF) Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) algorithm. A variable-length, controllable-precision FFT processor is proposed. The processor can perform 16, 64, 256 and 1024 point FFT/IFFT and provide flexible wordlength scaling modes for different FFT stages. Thus, the processor is suitable for different precision and FFT length requirements in various applications. Aiming at high throughput performance, single-path delay feedback (SDF) pipeline architecture is adopted. The design is testified on Xilinx Virtex6 xc6vcx240t FPGA. Accordingly, we make a clear comparison between the proposed design and Xilinx FFT v7.1. Our design achieves better signal-to-quantizationnoise ratio (SQNR) property and shorter pipeline latency. Meanwhile, the occupied resource is approximately the same. Moreover, SQNR performance of different FFT length and wordlength scaling modes is analysed.

articleTitle: Adaptive beamforming technique based on compressed sensing in multi-carrier frequency MIMO HFSWR
abstract: For the purpose of improving angle resolution and reducing the physical size of the receive array, we used multicarrier frequency in MIMO HFSWR system. Thanks to the usage of large spaced carrier frequencies, better angle resolution is obtained due to a virtual sparse array with bigger aperture than the physical real array, but high slop lobe appears as a drawback. Because of the angle of arriving signals is sparse, theory of compressed sensing (CS) theory is proposed to reconstruct the receiving signal from absence elements in the virtual sparse receive array. After that, adaptive digital beamforming techniques are adopted to form receive beams so as to make the main lobe of the beam point to the desired direction and nulls are steered to the interferences. Simulation results demonstrate that slop lobe is suppressed successfully and beam performances of the proposed method are comparable to that of virtual filled (Nyquist) array.

articleTitle: Space-varying atmospheric phase correction in ground-based SAR interferometry
abstract: Ground-based SAR(GB-SAR) is an important technical means in remote sensing deformation monitoring. However, atmospheric phase disturbances seriously affect the accuracy and reliability of the deformation retrieval. This paper improved the atmospheric phase correction algorithm proposed by Linhsia Noferini et al. and obtained a new atmospheric phase compensation algorithm based on corner reflection. The corner reflections were used to detect the strong permanent scatterers(PS) by double threshold detection method. Then the atmospheric phase screen can be got by interpolation and ploynomial fitting. After that, the corrected deformation phases also can be obtained. Finally, the slope deformation monitoring experiment was carried out to verify the feasibility and accuracy of the algorithm.

articleTitle: Emitter localization using signal waveform information in multistatic passive radar
abstract: This paper considers the localization of emitter by exploiting the prior information about signal waveforms to improve localization accuracy in the passive radar systems, configured with several distributed base stations. The received signals from all stations are jointly processed in a fusion center to directly estimate the position of emitter. Firstly a localization algorithm is proposed assuming that the signal waveform transmitted by the emitter is completely known. It is essentially a maximum-likelihood estimator by searching parameters of interest in a high-dimensional space. On the basis of above algorithm, we discussed the method using the prior information of signal waveforms to enhance the localization accuracy for the case of unknown signal waveforms. Simulation results show that all algorithms can provide robust and accurate position estimation of the emitter. The algorithm using signal waveform information is superior to the algorithm without regard to the information and more information of signal waveform is utilized the better localization performance is achieved.

articleTitle: A target detection method for non-cooperative PBR with frequency-agile and PRI-AGILE radar
abstract: In case of passive bistatic radar (PBR) using a phased array radar (PAR) as the non-cooperative illuminator, there are problems that signal parameters of the transmitter are unknown and signal coherence is damaged. Aiming at the issues, this article presents a target detection method for PBR using PAR as the non-cooperative illuminator. Firstly, the method uses the direct wave to estimate signal parameters, and then pulse compresses scattered wave. Secondly, the compressed wave is aligned by fast-time dimension so that a Range-Time (R-T) map can be obtained. Finally, the target is detected according to the trajectory in R-T map. The field experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of this method.

articleTitle: Waveform-agile sequential EKF for manoeuvrable target tracking
abstract: Since the cognitive radar was presented, dynamic waveform selection schemes have provided the optimal transmitted or received waveforms under certain criteria, based on the prior information of the target and environment, achieving the tracking performance improvement. This adaptive waveform solution has been paid more and more attention as advances in modern information processing techniques and devices enable its realization. In this paper, some improvements has been made to the existing dynamic waveform selection algorithms according to predecessor's work. The relationship between waveform parameters and tracking mean square error (MSE) is established through resolution cell and measurement extraction cell. According to this, the parameter of CF-HFM combined waveforms can be dynamically chosen to form the optimal transmitted waveform. A sequential extended kalman filter (SEKF) with Doppler measurements is used to track the manoeuvrable target. When the measurement model is nonlinear, this kind of selection and tracking algorithm can predict the target state directly thus reduce the computation. The proposed algorithm is validated to enhance the tracking performance by Monte Carlo simulations.

articleTitle: Parametric sparse representation method for parameter estimation in SAR imaging
abstract: For high resolution SAR focusing, a SAR parameter estimation method based on parametric sparse representation is proposed. The SAR echo is formulated as a parametric joint-sparse signal and the velocity of the platform is estimated by solving a joint optimization problem through iterative process. Compared to the phase difference (PD) method, the precision of estimation result is significantly improved with a smaller number of measurements. With the estimated velocity, a clearer image can be obtained. Experimental results on simulations and real data have shown the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Through-wall imaging by TE and TM hybrid polarization inversion based on FDFD and frequency hopping scheme
abstract: In this paper, TE and TM hybrid polarization contrast source inversion (CSI) based on FDFD and frequency hopping scheme is applied to through-wall imaging (TWI). The through-wall configuration is incorporated as a priori information in the background configuration of our FDFD inversion scheme. Multiple frequencies are used to improve the imaging performance. As the permittivity and conductivity of the targets are always higher than those of the air, the positivity of the contrast is utilized as a priori information to enhance the inversion performance. 2D simulation results show that the permittivity and conductivity of the targets behind the wall can be well reconstructed.

articleTitle: The identification of radar turbulence clutter based on connected-component analysis
abstract: The turbulence clutter may appear in the radar real detecting surrounding from seasons to seasons. The turbulence clutter has motion and Doppler shift. Furthermore, it is normally densely distributed but the single turbulence is small and similar to the target, so that it may cause serious influence on the target detection. This paper proposes a novel method for the identification of turbulence clutter based on connected-component analysis (CCA). The method can effectively identify the region contained turbulence clutter, which can be used to reduce the false alarms of radar detection. Finally, the results of both the simulation and real measured data are provided to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Higher-order MoM combined waveport analysis of circular waveguide problems
abstract: In this paper, the radiation problem of circular waveguide is analyzed using higher-order Method of Moments (MoM). The difficulty of the problem is the lack of matched excitations and loads. The method of mode matching is used to construct ideal waveports, which can provide not only excitations as sources but also perfectly matched loads. The involvement of Bessel functions makes the circular wave port more complicate. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed method can accurately and efficiently solve the circular waveguide problems. Finally, an electrically large reflector antenna is solved.

articleTitle: Low rank reconstruction algorithm for ground penetrating radar linear inverse imaging
abstract: In recent years, low rank matrix theory becomes one of the research hotspots in the image processing field. In this report, we construct a linear equation via born approximation for the electromagnetic inverse scattering problem, then solve the linear equation with Low Rank Constraint. The low rank matrix representation is applied to quickly and precisely reconstruct the low rank data matrix in GPR imaging. Simulation results and performance analysis show that Low Rank Reconstruction helps to reduce the memory space and computational complexity in GPR imaging.

articleTitle: Fast raw signal simulation based on equivalent scatterer and subaperture processing for one-stationary bistatic SAR
abstract: A fast raw signal simulation method based on the equivalent scatterer and subaperture processing for the one-stationary bistatic synthetic aperture radar (OS-BSAR) is presented. It considers the radar's motion error to simulate the more accuracy raw signal. First, the OS-BSAR geometry is built in elliptical polar coordinate, and then the scene is divided into several equidistant elliptical rings. Based on the equivalent scatterer, the approximate SAR system transfer function is derived, thus each pulse's raw signal is calculated by the convolution of the transmitted signal and transfer function, using the fast Fourier transform (FFT). To further improve the simulation speed, the subaperture and subscene processing are used. The transfer function for the same subaperture's pulses is calculated by the weighted sum of all the subscenes' equivalent scattering coefficient in the same equidistant elliptical ring, using the nonuniform FFT (NUFFT). This method involves NUFFT, FFT and complex multiplication, which means the easier operation and higher speed. Implementation of the proposed method is discussed. Simulation is given to prove the validity of the proposed method.

articleTitle: An ultra-wide band exponential flared TEM horn antenna for impulse radar systems
abstract: An ultra-broad band transverse electromagnetic(TEM) exponential horn antenna is designed. A balun is used for the impedance taper along the length of the proposed antenna to improve the antennas impedance characteristic and adapting an unbalanced plane line to a balanced one. The antenna is fabricated and tested. Broadband attributes are demonstrated with measured return loss of better than -10 dB from 8 to 20 GHZ.

articleTitle: Study on the echo signal model and R-D imaging algorithm for FMCW SAR
abstract: Frequency modulation continuous wave (FMCW) is often applied in miniature synthetic aperture radar (MINI SAR) . FMCW SAR sends linear frequency modulated (LFM) continuous wave signal with wide band, and the receiving echo of targets mixes with the sending signal. Therefore, the echo for imaging processing can be sampled in intermediate frequency (IF) band with low sampling rate, and the system can keep small and light. After imaging processing with the echos, FMCW SAR can obtain the image of the target with high resolution. In this paper, the observation geometry and the echo signal model of FMCW SAR are analyzed. Range-Doppler (R-D) algorithm for FMCW SAR imaging is deduced. Finally, the simulation experiments with R-D algorithm for point targets are given.

articleTitle: Clutter cancellation algorithm based on sparse auxiliary arrays
abstract: Adaptive sidelobe cancellation is one of the most effective ways to restrain active jamming, which uses the relationship among jamming signals to form beam pattern nulls in the directions of jamming by assisted receive channels. Thus the sidelobe active disturbance can be reduced significantly. This paper introduced the basic theories of ASLC and the basic requirements of auxiliary antenna's position firstly. And then this paper is primarily targeted to put forward a reasonable layout of the sparse auxiliary array to counteract the interferences well. And the research is unfolded from two aspects: array resolution and spatial fuzzy. Finally the computer simulation results demonstrated the correctness and validity of the related conclusions.

articleTitle: Analysis on guidance performance based on geostationary broadcast satellite
abstract: The space-based passive radar provides a greatly improved capability for worldwide surveillance and anti-radiation missiles, compared with terrestrial and airborne based system. It is the purpose of this paper to discuss the system performance, technology characteristics of passive bistatic radar based on space-based illuminators. A preliminary guidance performance evaluation of this type of radar is conducted in this paper, which is shown that target detection can be achieved with reliable performance. In addition, a detailed analysis of the resolution characteristics and ambiguity function are discussed, which can provide detection accuracy on the mid-course guidance. And system analyses are performed to identify the best candidate configurations and to estimate the capabilities of this type of radar.

articleTitle: Doppler frequency analysis of ground clutter for space-air based bistatic radar
abstract: Doppler frequency of ground clutter is an important parameter for bistatic radar. To study the variation of Doppler frequency, we give a detailed analysis of Doppler frequency for space-air based bistatic radar in this paper. Based on the geometric model of space-air based bistatic radar, the calculation formula of Doppler frequency is discussed, and the effects on changes of the space-air based platform flight direction and transmitting-receiving sphere centre angle are analysed. The Doppler frequency variation of local clutter scattering point is also studied. The analysis results show that the Doppler frequency of ground clutter is mainly influenced by the space-based platform motion and is related with the space-air based platform configuration.

articleTitle: PPP technique evaluation based its all estimates utilizing CSRS-PPP online service
abstract: This paper will address issues related to Precise Point Positioning (PPP) and perform raw observation data analysis to evaluate the specific performance of PPP based its all solutions processed by CSRS-PPP using final precise orbit and clock products from IGS. For this purpose, daily sessions of observations, at 30 seconds intervals, of five different IGS stations are processed using aforementioned approach. The tests show that, the solution accuracy reaches averagely 0.0023 m, -0.0005 m, -0.0035 m for static mode and about 5 cm for kinematic mode, respectively; centimeter convergence is obtained after being processed for 10-20 min, and residuals are nearly close to true-value after 30 min or more longer; tropospheric zenith delay estimates, both for static and kinematic, are greatly consistent with the solutions from IGS, and fluctuate within 5 mm; the residuals for clock offset are approximate to 0.1 ns about 1 h later, and the final values are close to 0 for three stations. It also may be inferred that carrier-phase ambiguity, real or integer, can play a pivotal role in aforementioned solutions.

articleTitle: Moving target location by low frequency single-channel SAR
abstract: The moving target in low frequency SAR is usually flooded in the clutter spectrum and has low SCR (signal to clutter ratio). Furthermore locating moving target in the single-channel low frequency SAR (Synthetic Aperture Radar) will meet the problem of “azimuth position uncertainty”. This paper solved this problem by the azimuth antenna pattern. It deduces the relationship between the 2dimensional spectrum of moving target and azimuth antenna pattern. The proposed method uses a relative endpoint of Doppler spectrum to estimate moving target parameters to locate moving target at constant velocity. It has low computation load and is suitable for SCR above -20dB. Simulation results illustrate the effective performance of this method.

articleTitle: A novel Bayesian adaptive detector against non-Gaussian clutter
abstract: We present a novel two-step radar signal detector against the non-Gaussian distributed clutter in this paper. The compound Gaussian distribution is employed to model the clutter, which describes the clutter vector as the product of a non-negative random variable (the so-called texture) with a complex Gaussian random vector (called the speckle). The posteriori probability density function of the texture parameter is given by the Bayesian approach using a non-informative priori. Then the expression of testing statistic is derived according to likelihood ratio test rules. The Monte Carlo simulation is taken to investigate the performance of the detector in several kinds of clutter environments and the results show its improvement compared to the conventional adaptive matched filter detector.

articleTitle: Submillimetric motion detection with a 94 GHZ ground based synthetic aperture radar
abstract: The paper presents the validation and experimental assessment of a 94 GHz (W-Band) CW-FM Radar that can be configured as a Ground Based SAR for high resolution imaging and interferometry. Several experimental campaigns have been carried out to assess the capability of the system to remotely observe submillimetric deformation and vibration in infrastructures.

articleTitle: The implement of spaceborne SAR imaging system
abstract: With the rapid development of FPGA parallel processing and DSP float-point computing capability, FPGA and DSP play an increasingly important role in the field of high-speed real-time synthetic aperture radar (SAR) signal processing system. In this letter, based on the SAR imaging needs and principles, taking chirp scaling algorithm for example, we design a spaceborne SAR real-time imaging heterogeneous system implemented by FPGA and DSP. The heterogeneous system uses modular thinking, pipeline and parallel processing techniques, which greatly improves the speed and operation precision in SAR imaging. Besides, the SAR imaging system has a good realtime performance, scalability and faulty tolerance and can well meet the needs of spaceborne SAR imaging system. The system needs 19.72s to generate a 4096*4096 pixel image.

articleTitle: A near-field back-projection algorithm for wall penetrating SAR
abstract: We are going to develop a handheld wall penetrating SAR (WPSAR) to investigate the small shallowly buried objects such as thin wires, cables and so on. The WPSAR will be working very close to the wall surface, and the objects of interest sometimes buried inside the induced near-filed region of the probe. As a result, the traditional far-field SAR imaging algorithm cannot be used. Thus, a useful near-field back-projection algorithm is investigated in this paper, which backprojects the probe's aperture field into the wall, instead of backprojecting the echo signal along the wave propagation track as it is done in the traditional BP. A full wave simulation data given by CST is used to validate our algorithm. The result shows that the proposed near-field BP algorithm gives a correct imaging result while the traditional one fails.

articleTitle: Double image encryption based on the random fractional transform
abstract: This paper proposes a method for double image encryption based on a proposed random fractional transform. Firstly, we produce a pseudorandom sequence to randomize the eigenvalue of the discrete fractional Fourier transform based on logistic map. Secondly, a random matrix is produced based on two-dimension logistic map. Then, the eigenvector of the proposed random matrix is used to replace the eigenvector of the discrete fractional Fourier transform. At the last, we present a double image encryption algorithm based on the proposed random fractional transform. Numerical simulations have been performed to verify the efficiency of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Enhanced monopulse angle estimation using 4-channel radar system
abstract: This paper describes a 4-channel monopulse radar system with an additional delta-delta beam. This additional degree-of-freedom can be used to provide advanced capabilities such as mainlobe jamming cancellation, 2-target main beam resolution and enhanced angle estimation using 2 sets of monopulse ratios. The 4-channel system provides two sets of monopulse ratios which complement each other and as a result, angle estimation accuracy is improved with mitigation of beam-shape loss.

articleTitle: Airborne ISAR imaging to air target
abstract: Conventional ground-based ISAR is restrained by the noncooperative motion of targets and has long coherent processing interval (CPI), so its imaging performance is unstable. In this work airborne ISAR imaging technique will be discussed, which can shorten the distance from radar to air target, decrease the CPI, and improve imaging applicability. Firstly, the relative motion between radar and the air target is analyzed. Secondly, the imaging model is built and a whole matched filtering (WMF) imaging algorithm is proposed. Finally, the multi-focus processing is expatiated, the radar flight error is analyzed and the method that adjusting radar flight perimeters to improve the reality imaging quality is discussed.

articleTitle: Spaceborne radar-communication integration signal design for moving target detection
abstract: The satellite signal design of radar-communication integration employing OFDM frame is studied. Satellite communication and moving target detection is accomplished simultaneously using the signal we designed in this paper. The questions on how to choose OFDM modulation parameters which affect both radar and communication are analyzed. The signal design criteria are not only accuracy of distance and speed measurements for radar sensing but also data rate and data error rate for communication channel. Finally, an optimum solution for both applications is proposed and its simulations for moving target detection and image transmission indicate the practical feasibility of radar-communication integration.

articleTitle: Spatial spectrum estimation based on compressive sensing
abstract: The most prominent subspace decomposition methods for spatial spectrum estimation include multiple signal classification algorithm (MUSIC) as well as estimation signal parameter via rotational invariance technique (ESPRIT). However, the drawbacks of MUSIC is that estimating the number of source signals are constraint by the following two aspects: array aperture and a large number of sampling data. After carefully investigating the theory of compressive sensing (CS), this paper constructs the model for spatial spectrum estimation on the basis of the sparsity of source signals in the angle spectrum. According to the principle of CS, spatial signals can be sampled with much less sensors, which leads to small sampling data. Furthermore, the source signals can be reconstructed accurately by some recovery algorithms. The approaches are compared with MUSIC and three numerical simulation experiments are programmed with MATLAB. The reconstruction results are found to be approximately to the original signals. The most attractive merits of our proposed method not only reduces the number of elements which are needed for sampling as well as decreases the amount of sampling data, but also the source signals can be reconstructed in terms of their amplitude and bearing simultaneously.

articleTitle: Modified spatial clutter sparsity estimation for closely-spaced target tracking
abstract: The number of targets and the origin of measurement point are uncertain in target tracking, and measurement origins are always prior unknown. An accurate estimation result of clutter measurement density can provide a significant benefit in target tracking. However, the measurements caused by target give a bias of the clutter measurement density estimation, especially in the situation of closely-spaced target tracking. In this paper we proposed a new unbiased method to eliminate the effect of measurements from target and improve the performance of target tracking, the new method is a modification on spatial clutter measurement sparsity estimator. In the new method we subtract the probability of target existence from the number of measurement we used for clutter density estimation in order to get the unbiased estimation of clutter intensity. The simulation study results validate the effectiveness of the proposed new method.

articleTitle: A novel frequency discrimination method based on all phase FFT for anti-towed decoy
abstract: This paper proposes a novel frequency discrimination method and discusses its application on anti-towed decoy. Before describing the proposed method, the principle of all phase FFT is first introduced. Then, based on the property of phase invariant, a novel frequency discrimination method based on all phase FFT is presented. Furthermore, the performance is specifically analyzed via numerical experiments to demonstrate the advantages of all phase FFT. Compared with the conventional method, the proposed method has higher frequency resolution and is more suitable for distinguishing the target from the towed decoy. Simulation results verify the validity of the proposed method and show the good performance in anti-towed decoy jamming.

articleTitle: The research on the effects of an active FSS with circle element on the characteristics of radar absorbing materials
abstract: An active frequency selective surface (FSS) is designed, and is combined with Radar Absorbing Materials to form a composite absorbing structure. Based on the equivalent theory that the PIN diode can be regarded as resistance, the voltage-loading resistance of active FSS element is researched for RAM containing FSS, and the electromagnetic wave reflectivity performance is analyzed. The influence of active FSS design parameters on the reflectivity of RAM is researched, and the FSS design parameters include the voltage-loading manner, the resistance parameter, and the position in the RAM. The research result shows that the resonance frequency of RAM containing FSS can be dynamically adjusted from 3GHz to 4GHz by changing voltage-loading resistance of active FSS, and the reflectivity can be reduced from -13dB to -35dB.

articleTitle: A cross-range scaling approach for ISAR image of aircraft with large propellers
abstract: The aircraft is a common type of target in the inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) imaging. The size is a key parameter for aircraft recognition whereas it cannot be obtained directly from the ISAR image where the crossrange resolution is not easy to get. Cross-range scaling approaches should be developed. However, some aircrafts are equipped with large propellers whose echoes may induce the micro-Doppler effect which will cover the body scatters and make some previous cross-range scaling approaches invalid in the practice. In this paper, the parameter difference between propeller signals and body signals are analysed, and based on the adaptive chirplet decomposition, a proper approach for the ISAR image of aircraft with large propellers, which can separate body signals from propeller signals and exactly estimate the crossrange resolution simultaneously is presented. The appropriateness determination method of thresholds for signal separation is also proposed. The validity is demonstrated by processing results of simulated data and real data.

articleTitle: A multipath exploitation technique for SAR in strong point scattering environment
abstract: Conventional synthetic aperture radars (SAR) which implicitly assume direct path scattering mechanism fail to deal with complicated multipath scenario. This paper presents an innovative compressive sensing based multipath exploitation imaging technique for the point scattering multipath scenario. The proposed technique makes use of prior information of the location of point scatter and establishes an omni-directional scattering multipath model to depict the scenario. Based on the model, an over complete dictionary that account for interaction of the radar, targets and environment can be constructed. The image reconstruction is implemented with the CS technique by solving a convex optimization problem. The proposed technique can effectively solve the target image from each scattering path and at the same time, can significantly reduce data recording time. The new technique is validated by numeric simulations.

articleTitle: Multi-resolution composite array based radar with adaptive beamforming
abstract: This paper presents a novel multi-resolution composite array (MRCA) based Radar for high resolution digital beamforming (DBF) with much less elements than conventional uniform linear array. An adaptive beamforming based multi-targets distinguish scheme is proposed to improve multi-targets detection ability of MRCA based radar in a wide direction region. Adaptive MRCA examples were investigated with simulations to verify our radar system and show the effectiveness.
